AO-01 Premium Clinical Skincare Brand — Product-Shot Finishing, Logo Vectorization, Per-SKU Label Merge & Print-Ready Packaging Export
Photo & Image Beauty, Cosmetics & Personal Care 20 calls 8 outputs 17 checks · 9a/8e ▼
Take our raw skincare hero shot, flat logo mark, texture plate and SKU copy sheet and produce a clinically clean white-background product image set, an editable vector logo, a recommended type system, a packaging-safe wide landscape reframe of the hero (cropped from the pure-white-sweep master), a clinical monochrome variant, per-SKU print labels merged from our label template, and a print-ready packaging PDF.
Full brief
We're launching DERMAVERA, a premium clinically-tested skincare line, and need a cohesive, credible visual identity executed across the product line (3 launch SKUs: a Vitamin-C Serum, a Barrier Repair Cream, and a Gentle Gel Cleanser). The look must be clean, minimalist, modern, science-driven and trustworthy — premium without being flashy, professional without looking pharmaceutical. We are supplying: (1) one raw hero photograph of the Serum bottle shot on a near-white sweep (slightly tilted, mixed lighting, cluttered edges); (2) a flat high-res raster of our chosen logo mark (a minimal molecule/droplet monogram + "DERMAVERA" wordmark) that we need delivered as a clean editable vector; (3) a soft lifestyle texture plate (matte stone surface) for collateral grounding; (4) a label-copy spreadsheet with one row per SKU (name, claim, volume, INCI line, batch placeholder, hex accent). We also supply our pre-authored print templates: an Illustrator label template (label.ai) with genuine Variables, and an InDesign unit-carton template (carton.pdf). Deliverables: a flawless clinical white-background hero image (straightened, background swept to pure white, neutral clinical color, crisp product), a 1:1 e-commerce crop and a packaging-safe wide landscape reframe of the hero cropped to the target 5000×2800px (the pure-white-sweep master crop-and-resized to the wider ratio, centered on the product — sweep trimmed top/bottom, no canvas added), a clinical monochrome (single-accent duotone) brand variant of the hero, the logo delivered as an editable SVG, a recommended display+text type pairing, a print-ready per-SKU label set generated by merging our copy sheet into label.ai, and a print-ready packaging PDF exported from carton.pdf. Everything must be print-ready and leave us editable source (vector SVG + the authored .ai/.indd). Maintain consistent neutral, trustworthy color across every image.

AO-02 Performance-ready Meta ad product creatives: white-bg clean-up, brand color grade, multi-ratio reframe set, and vectorized logo for paid-social testing
Photo & Image E-commerce, Retail & Product 19 calls 7 outputs 14 checks · 9a/5e ▼
Turn the client's raw product shot and logo into a performance-ready Meta ad creative kit: a retouched pure-white-bg hero, a brand-graded variant, three platform-ratio frames (1:1 / 4:5 / 9:16) built by honestly cropping/reframing the graded hero to each ratio, a vectorized logo, and a font direction to steer the handed-off typeset step.
Full brief
DONE is a DTC homeware brand launching paid-social tests for its matte-ceramic pour-over coffee dripper and needs a freelancer to build the imagery layer of a Meta (Facebook + Instagram) ad-creative kit, faithful to the brand guidelines (brand teal #0F6E64 on warm off-white #F4EFE7). You are supplied three client assets: (1) a raw studio product photo of the dripper on a near-white sweep that still shows seamless-paper shadows and a faint gray cast; (2) the DONE wordmark logo as a flat PNG; and (3) the brand-guideline sheet as a PDF for reference.

Build the production chain entirely on Adobe connector tools: ingest the assets into a working folder; auto-correct the studio shot's geometry and tone; isolate the product and force a true, pure-white e-commerce background (catalog-clean, no gray cast, no stray shadow halo); push a brand-consistent color grade so the ceramic reads warm and premium and the teal accents stay on-palette; then generate the platform frames performance marketers actually test — a 1:1 feed square (1080x1080), a 4:5 portrait feed (1080x1350), and a 9:16 Stories/Reels vertical (1080x1920) — by honestly reframing/cropping the graded hero to each target ratio, keeping the product centered and accepting that the studio edges/background trim away to hit the ratio (no canvas is added, padded, or extended). Separately, vectorize the supplied wordmark to a clean SVG so it stays crisp at any ad size.

Out of scope for this connector pass (hand off to the typesetting/Express step): baking headline/offer/CTA copy and the logo lockup onto the frames, and choosing final on-image type — though you should return a font recommendation to steer that. Deliverables: the pure-white hero, the brand-graded hero, the three ratio frames (1:1 / 4:5 / 9:16), the vector logo, and the font direction.

AO-03 E-commerce white-background product retouch suite + vectorized brand mark
Photo & Image E-commerce, Retail & Product 17 calls 4 outputs 14 checks · 9a/5e ▼
Turn a client's raw, messy-background product photo into a pure-white-background marketplace catalog image and convert their rough hand-drawn logo sketch into a clean, brand-colored, scalable vector logo — then package everything for delivery.
Full brief
Our small skincare-and-homeware shop is scaling onto Amazon, Etsy and our own Shopify store and we badly need visual credibility — right now our listings use phone snaps shot on a kitchen table and they look amateur, which is killing conversion. We can't afford a studio day, so we're sending you what we have: RAW product captures (a high-resolution amber-glass serum bottle shot handheld under window light on a cluttered wooden table, slightly tilted) and a rough logo: our founder hand-inked our brand mark "AURELIA BOTANICALS" on paper and we photographed it with a phone — it's wonky, grey-ish, on off-white paper.

We need you to do the full product-photographer post-production pass and the logo cleanup:

PRODUCT IMAGE (do this as a repeatable recipe — we'll send 10-15 more bottles and jars that all must match):
- Level the horizon (the table edge is tilted).
- Cut the bottle off the messy table and put it on a PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF) seamless background, which is the hard requirement for Amazon's main-image policy.
- Deliver it as a square 1400×1400 px marketplace canvas with the product centered.
- Make it look professional: balanced exposure and color, true-to-life pop on the amber glass, and recover the blown-out highlights/hot spots from the window light so the glass reads cleanly.

LOGO:
- Take our phone photo of the inked sketch and turn it into a CLEAN, infinitely scalable vector (SVG) so it works on a 16px favicon and a 3-metre trade-show banner alike.
- Recolor the mark to our brand green (deep botanical green ~#1E5E3A).
- Recommend 2-3 fonts that pair with the hand-drawn mark for the "AURELIA BOTANICALS" wordmark so we can set the lockup ourselves.

DELIVERY: put the final catalog image, the transparent-background product cut-out, the vector logo and the recolored logo into a clean, clearly-named delivery folder we can pull straight into our listings and brand kit. Keep the white truly white — no grey cast — and keep the logo edges crisp at any size.

AO-04 Silver Jewelry iPhone Shots to White-Background E-commerce Set (JPEG + transparent PNG)
Photo & Image Fashion & Apparel 15 calls 3 outputs 13 checks · 7a/6e ▼
Turn a handheld iPhone shot of a silver jewellery piece into a clean, colour-accurate, uniform-white e-commerce set: a 2000x2000 sRGB JPEG plus a matching transparent PNG, ready to slot straight into the online store.
Full brief
I run a silver jewellery line and need my iPhone-captured product frames turned into a polished, store-ready e-commerce set through AI-powered post-production. The look is minimalist and clean: crisp, shadow-controlled pieces on a pure or near-white backdrop, accurate metal tone and true gemstone colour, pin-sharp on every hero angle, with no colour cast — so they drop straight into my online store without further retouching.

Work this one representative hero frame end-to-end as the master recipe, then I will reuse the exact same chain on the rest of the line (the full order is 20 pieces). Start from the original iPhone HEIC/RAW file I supply. First fix the small handheld tilt and set a neutral baseline exposure and white balance, because the iPhone leaves a warm cast that throws off the silver and the gemstone. Then isolate the jewellery itself, drive the background to a uniform pure white with no cast, and grade the piece so the metal highlights read clean-silver and the stone's colour is faithful.

Deliverables for this frame: one finished JPEG at exactly 2000 x 2000 px, sRGB, on uniform white; and one matching PNG of the same piece on a fully transparent background for layering on coloured store sections. Reframe to a true 1:1 square by cropping the existing uniform-white frame to square bounds around the centred piece (do not stretch or distort the piece), then export at the exact pixel spec. Finally, organise the outputs into a tidy delivery folder for client download.

Acceptance: uniform white background, no colour cast; accurate metal tone and gemstone colour; pin-sharp focus on the hero angle; exact 2000 x 2000 sRGB JPEG plus matching transparent PNG.

AO-06 White-Background Catalog Cleanup for a Firearms/Optics/Outdoor Shopify Store
Photo & Image Nonprofit, Religious & Community 12 calls 5 outputs 13 checks · 7a/6e ▼
Take a batch of inconsistent distributor-supplied product photos for a firearms/optics/outdoor Shopify store and turn them into clean, straightened, color-corrected, pure-white-background, square marketplace hero images (plus transparent-PNG tile variants and a vectorized listing badge).
Full brief
I run a hands-off Shopify store selling thermal cameras, night-vision optics, firearms, ammunition, trail-camera mounts and hunting accessories. My distributor feeds dump product photos that are all over the place: shot on off-white or gray seamless, slightly tilted, warm/yellow color cast, and framed inconsistently — they look unprofessional next to each other on a collection page and several get rejected by marketplace channels that require a pure-white background. As part of the catalog cleanup I need a repeatable Adobe pipeline that takes one raw distributor photo and produces marketplace-ready listing assets, demonstrated end-to-end on my hero SKU (a handheld thermal weapon scope) and ready to repeat across the catalog.

For the hero SKU, starting from the single raw distributor JPEG I provide, deliver: (1) a corrected master — auto-straightened, cropped to the product, exposure/tone normalized, and the warm color cast neutralized; (2) a pure #FFFFFF background version where the scope is isolated and the messy seamless is replaced with solid white per Shopify/Amazon hero spec; (3) a transparent-PNG cut-out of the same scope for collection tiles and bundle mock-ups; (4) a square 1:1 hero produced by cropping the white-background hero to a centered 1:1 square (the source frame is portrait, so the square is a crop of the existing image — no canvas is invented or extended) and then resized/exported at exactly 1400×1400. Also vectorize the small distributor brand badge I supply (a flat single-color logo mark) into a clean SVG so it scales on the listing.

Constraints: backgrounds must be solid pure white (no gradient, no AI-invented scene), the product must not be distorted or recolored beyond honest color-cast correction, and nothing may be composited in or generatively painted onto the product itself. Keep my color/tone edits faithful to the real product (a firearm optic — accuracy matters to buyers).

AO-12 Bright-and-Airy Lightroom Grade for a 38-Shot Food Photography Set (Flat-Lay, 45°, Side)
Photo & Image Food, Restaurant & Beverage 17 calls 5 outputs 14 checks · 6a/8e ▼
Take a client's 38-frame food shoot (flat-lay / 45° / side of one dish) that is close to the mark and grade it to a cohesive bright-and-airy look — white balance, exposure, highlight/shadow, gentle color — then deliver straightened, correctly-sized final files.
Full brief
A food-photography client (single hero dish, shot three ways: an overhead flat-lay, a 45-degree three-quarter, and a side/profile shot, 38 frames total) hands you a set that is "close to the goal but needs tweaking." The goal is a consistent BRIGHT AND AIRY look across the whole set: clean neutral-to-slightly-warm white balance, lifted exposure, bright but not blown highlights on the plate and window light, open (not muddy) shadows, and gentle, appetising color — applied cohesively so the 38 frames read as one shoot. Quick turnaround / ASAP.

Concretely, working in the Adobe connector entirely on the client's own pixels (no compositing, no generative fill, no background swap):
1. Ingest the three representative hero frames the recipe is tuned on.
2. On the flat-lay, square it up (auto-straighten the overhead so the plate edges are true) and crop to a clean composition.
3. Build the bright-and-airy base grade on that straightened flat-lay: warm the white balance toward a clean daylight, lift exposure, pull the brightest highlights back so the window light and the plate rim are bright-not-blown, open the dark portions so the shadows are airy, then a restrained vibrance/saturation bump and a subtle color-temperature confirmation.
4. Selectively brighten the dish itself: prompt-select the food to build a mask and apply a small targeted highlight/exposure lift through that mask so the hero pops without crushing the airy backdrop.
5. Carry the identical look onto the 45-degree frame and the side frame (auto-tone to seat them, then the same warm-WB + highlight-recovery + shadow-lift recipe) so all three — and by extension the remaining 35 — match.
6. Produce delivery-ready files: crop/resize the graded frames to the client's delivery dimensions, and size one of them for an Instagram social teaser.

Deliverables: the three fully-graded hero frames at delivery resolution, the selective-food-pop master, and an Instagram-sized teaser — all unified to one cohesive bright-and-airy look.

Prep and deliver the campaign-ready photo + brand asset pack (retouched, warm/bold-graded hero food shots, color-splash and subject-pop scroll-stop variants, cut-out dishes, three Meta ad ratios via reframe-crop, a licensed backdrop texture, and a vectorized logo) for a West Palm Beach Mexican restaurant's Taco Tuesday & Lunch-Special Meta ad mockups.
Full brief
You are the production designer prepping the photo and brand assets that will be dropped into 12 static Meta (Facebook/Instagram) ad mockups for a family-owned, authentic Mexican restaurant in West Palm Beach, FL. The brand is warm, bold, family-oriented and community-focused — a local neighborhood favorite, NOT a corporate chain. The campaign covers two offers: Taco Tuesday (scroll-stop, urgent, recurring-promo feel) and Lunch Specials. The client has supplied three raw phone/DSLR food photos (a hero al-pastor taco platter, a carne-asada lunch plate, a margarita-and-chips table scene), plus their logo as a flat PNG.

Your job, entirely within the Adobe connector:
1) Load the three supplied food photos and the logo PNG into the project.
2) Straighten and tonally fix the hero taco shot (auto-straighten the slightly tilted handheld frame, then auto-tone), so it reads clean and appetizing.
3) Push a warm, bold restaurant grade on the corrected hero: lift color temperature toward warm, boost vibrance/saturation so the salsa reds and lime greens pop, and recover highlight detail on the glossy meat — the "appetizing and bold" look the brand wants.
4) Build a scroll-stop "color-splash" variant from the graded hero: select the taco/food by prompt, invert the selection so everything BUT the food is selected, and desaturate that background so the food is the only color on screen (eye-catching scroll-stop power).
5) Apply an Adaptive "Subject Pop" preset to the graded hero to create a second high-contrast scroll-stop variant with the food made to stand forward.
6) Create a clean cut-out of the lunch plate: remove the background to a transparent PNG so the dish can float on any colored ad background the layout team chooses.
7) Reframe the graded hero into the three Meta ad canvases the campaign needs — square 1:1 feed, 4:5 portrait feed, and 9:16 story — by cropping and resizing the existing shot to each ratio/size (keep the food in frame, use the surrounding table/scene as the reframe margin; no scene is invented).
8) License one on-brand backdrop texture (warm woven Mexican textile / rustic wood) from Adobe Stock at full res for the layout team to use behind cut-outs.
9) Vectorize the supplied logo PNG into a clean SVG so it scales crisply across every ad size.
10) Copy the final delivery set into a clearly named project folder for client handoff.

Deliverables: the corrected + warm-graded hero JPEG; the color-splash hero; the Subject-Pop hero; the transparent-PNG lunch-plate cut-out; three ratio-correct hero canvases (1:1, 4:5, 9:16); one licensed full-res backdrop texture; the logo SVG; and a named delivery folder containing the full set.

Work to perform with Adobe connectors:

You are the recurring post-production designer for "Princerrr," a daily-life vlog shot in 4K and delivered at 1080p. Full brief
A landlord listing a freshly renovated rental on Airbnb and Zillow has captured interior frames of the three key areas — living room, kitchen, and bedroom — during a 0700-1200 natural-light window, but the RAW-style frames are tilted, slightly under-exposed in the shadows, mixed-white-balance (warm tungsten vs cool window daylight), and carry minor wall scuffs and dust marks. They want the post-production handled to a "modern, clean, simple, ample lighting, natural" standard: straight verticals and distortion-free perspective, basic color correction, gentle shadow lift and highlight recovery so the rooms read bright and spacious, quick blemish spotting on wall scuffs/dust WITHOUT an over-processed look, and final files delivered in two formats per the brief — web-optimized JPEG under 2 MB each AND full-resolution PNG — within three days.

The freelancer must run an Adobe photo-editing chain per room: license/load the supplied frame, auto-straighten the verticals, crop out the resulting wedge to a clean distortion-free frame, apply auto-tone as a neutral baseline, neutralize the mixed white balance with a color-temperature correction, lift the dark portions and recover the blown window highlights, selectively brighten the room interior via a prompt-based mask so the space feels open without flattening the windows, spot-correct wall scuffs/dust by selecting the blemish and filling it with the matched neutral wall color (solid fill only — not generative), apply a final gentle vibrance/saturation lift for the "modern clean" feel, then crop-and-resize to the two delivery specs and deliver the corrected JPEG/PNG set for all three rooms. Across the three rooms the chain reuses the straighten→crop→tone→temperature→shadow/highlight→selective-brighten→spot-fix→vibrance→resize pattern, every step consuming the previous step's output.

Photo & Image Photo Editing, Retouching & Restoration 17 calls 2 outputs 13 checks · 4a/9e ▼
Digitize and restore one 1910 magician-troupe postcard — clarify and lighten the dark sepia front photo and sharpen the contrast of the handwritten back so the description is legible — and deliver each side as its own clean, deskewed, print-and-social-ready file.
Full brief
A family-history client is digitizing ~24 antique postcard photographs from 1910 documenting a famous stage magician and his traveling company touring Asia and abroad; the client's grandmother and aunt performed in the troupe and wrote a description of each scene on the BACK of the postcards. The client needs every postcard delivered as two separate restored files — the photographic FRONT as one picture and the handwritten BACK as another — that are clean enough to be pasted into a printed memorial book and posted to social media. Many of the front photos are dark, low-contrast, and tilted from flatbed scanning; the handwriting on the backs is faint cursive pencil/ink that is hard to read. This benchmark uses ONE representative postcard as the worked end-to-end example. The client supplies two raw flatbed scans: (1) the postcard front (a dark, slightly rotated sepia-toned albumen-style photograph of the magician and company on a theatre stage, with scanner-bed border) and (2) the postcard back (faded cursive handwriting plus a postmark and divided-back postcard printing, also slightly skewed). Required restoration pipeline, per side: ingest both raw scans into the workspace; auto-straighten each skewed scan and crop away the scanner-bed margins to the postcard edge; on the FRONT, recover the dark midtones and shadows, lift exposure and overall brightness/contrast, rein in any blown highlight on the bright stage lights, gently recover the crushed dark portions where the company stands in shadow, neutralize the scanner's cool cast and re-warm to a consistent archival sepia, and finish with a vintage-photo preset look that keeps the period feel while making faces and stage detail readable; on the BACK, push brightness and contrast hard and convert to a clean high-legibility monochrome/sepia so the faint cursive description reads clearly. Deliver a high-resolution restored FRONT and a high-resolution restored BACK, each deskewed and edge-cropped, color-consistent, copy-paste-ready for the book layout and for social posts.

They are pixelated mock-ups that cannot go to a mint. The task is to convert each into production-grade vector art and deliver a four-color family per mark.

Pipeline per the connector chain: (1) upload all five client rasters to CC storage and preview them; (2) on the primary logo, remove the busy background so only the mark survives on transparency; (3) auto-straighten the de-bagged logo so the mark sits square (coins are minted on a true axis); (4) crop the straightened logo tight to its own bounds so the trace has no dead margin; (5) reframe/resize that cropped mark to a fixed 2000x2000 px square proof canvas via image_crop_and_resize (a gen-free crop-and-scale to the target aspect — no pixels are invented), establishing the exact resolution every variant export inherits; (6) vectorize that clean, square, transparent master into a scalable SVG — this is the editable master vector that also seeds EPS/PDF on packaging; (7) select the mark's silhouette on the 2000x2000 master, then fill it with solid true-black to mint the BLACK variant; (8) on the same selected silhouette, fill it with solid white to mint the WHITE variant; (9) apply a flat color overlay in gold #C8A24B to mint the GOLD variant; (10) apply a monochromatic silver/gray tint to mint the SILVER variant. Then the four coin references are run through the same remove-background -> crop -> vectorize spine so all five marks are coin-ready vector. Finally, copy every produced vector + variant asset into a structured per-mark deliverables folder and package the full logo+four-coin family (SVG sources, transparent PNGs, black/white/gold/silver variants) into one ZIP for mint/manufacturer handoff.

Hard constraints honored: no from-scratch illustration (every mark is traced from a client reference), no generative fill / outpaint / object removal / compositing / upscaling; image_crop_and_resize only crops-and-scales the existing mark to the square proof canvas (it never grows or invents canvas), image_fill_area is used only for SOLID color minting (black and white) of an isolated mask, and no generative tool is used at any step. Deliverables map 1:1 to the brief: transparent PNGs, SVG vector source, and black/white/gold/silver color versions, coin-ready and readable at small sizes.

Full brief
HaulAway (junk removal & cleanout, Maitland FL / North Orlando) supplies ONE existing logo they love but only as a flat, low-resolution raster PNG (a bold "HA" monogram lockup with the company wordmark beneath, in their black / lime-green / gray palette). They need it turned into a professional, print-ready brand identity kit usable on t-shirts, vehicle & trailer wraps, car magnets, and print.

The freelancer must drive the Adobe Creative Cloud connector end-to-end:
1) Ingest the client's raster logo and get a clean working copy (auto-tone + straighten the slightly skewed scan so edges are true).
2) Clean the color: neutralize any off-cast and crisp up the lime green and the blacks so the trace is sharp.
3) Clean-knock the background to transparent so the trace has no halo.
4) Vectorize the cleaned full lockup into a clean SVG = the MASTER vector (basis for AI/EPS/SVG/PNG exports).

7) Build the layout LOCKUPS by cropping the cleaned master to its true bounds for the horizontal version and a tighter square for the stacked/vertical and the magnet.

Hard rules honored: ABSOLUTELY no generative fill, no AI object removal, no text-to-image, no compositing, no layout composition; image_fill_area is solid-color only; the master export step only EXPORTS genuine vector — the deliverable vector emerges from image_vectorize, not from an authored .ai. Full brief
A pool-design / pool-builder studio needs vector artwork of its swimming pools for the gallery and "Our Builds" pages of a new website. The client supplies three real photographs of completed pools — a freeform lagoon pool, a rectangular infinity-edge pool, and a kidney-shaped residential pool. Each must be "redrawn" as a high-quality, detailed vector image that accurately represents the pool, is visually appealing, and meets the site's clean, flat, modern standard.

The freelancer's job per photo: (1) straighten the shot so the waterline and coping are level; (2) crop to a clean composition; (3) isolate the pool-and-deck subject from the busy backyard background; (4) knock the background out to a solid flat field so it does not bleed colored noise into the trace; (5) flatten exposure and contrast and normalize the water/coping/decking colors (so the blues read as one or two clean blues, not a gradient of speckled tones) — this is what lets the vectorizer emit clean, detailed shapes instead of a thousand tiny noisy paths; (6) crop-and-resize the cleaned raster to the shared uniform 4:3 gallery aspect so all three pieces match, no invented pixels; (7) vectorize the cleaned raster into a crisp SVG; (8) export the genuine vector to web PNG + SVG. The three finished vectors and their matching web PNGs are collected into a delivery project folder for the website handoff.

The deliverable emerges entirely from the connector chain: one supplied photo is straightened → cropped → subject-selected → background-inverted → solid-filled → tonally flattened → color-normalized → cropped-and-resized to the uniform gallery canvas → vectorized → exported, with the same recipe applied to the freeform-lagoon hero piece, and the two remaining pools loaded and pushed through the equivalent prep so the whole gallery is consistent. Output is a uniform set of three flat-color pool vectors (SVG + flat-white-background web PNG) collected into a delivery project folder.

From the approved folk-art 20th-Anniversary master, produce a print-ready 5-screen separation pack (white underbase + four spot-colour halftone plates with a dot-gain choke), a vectorized hard-edge lettering/line plate, a grain-textured client proof, and the registration/separation sheet rendered out of the supplied Illustrator template (PDF and SVG as two separate render passes).
Full brief
Bayou Cross Classical Academy (a classical Christian school in the fictional town of Sainte-Colombe, Louisiana) has APPROVED the final folk-art / festival-poster illustration celebrating the school's first twenty years — a handcrafted, story-driven composition weaving faith, academics, student life, community traditions, and campus landmarks, rich with discoverable details. The illustration phase is complete and signed off; this engagement is the screen-print PRODUCTION phase. You are given: (1) the approved master artwork as a high-resolution flattened RGB PNG (portrait 2:3, full-bleed, at the master's native raster resolution), in which the figurative folk-art scene carries soft tonal passages and the commemorative title/year lettering is hard-edge solid; (2) the campus reference photos that accompanied the creative brief (chapel, oak quad, schoolhouse facade, founding-class photo); and (3) the print shop's authored Illustrator separation/registration sheet template (separations.ai) carrying real artboards, registration marks, and ink-name slots.

Deliver a 5-screen spot-colour separation pack for a manual screen print on natural/cream stock: a WHITE UNDERBASE plate (solid fill behind all art), and four spot-ink plates — Marian Blue, Antique Gold, Brick Red, and Ink Black — where the continuous-tone folk-art passages are converted to a registered Ben-Day halftone dot field and CHOKED (a light blur pass on the dot layer tightens the dot edges) so dots do not plug on press, while the title lettering and key line-work stay hard-edge solid via a vectorized hold-out plate. Because image_vectorize traces a whole raster and has no mask input, first knock the figurative art field out to flat with a solid fill (leaving only the masked lettering/line-work on the canvas), then vectorize that lettering-only raster to the crisp hold-out SVG. Symmetrically, because image_apply_halftone is a whole-image effect that exposes no mask parameter, prepare the mirror-image raster first — solid-fill the lettering region flat to leave an art-field-only raster — and then screen that raster, so the dot field covers only the figurative passages and the type is never dotted. Provide a single flattened grain-textured client proof that previews the screen-print \"tooth\" on cream stock, and the registration/separation sheet rendered out of the supplied Illustrator template as two separate export passes (PDF and SVG — document_render_vector emits one media type per call). Every separation must share identical trim and registration so the five screens line up on the press.

Full brief
We run a personal-training business with a library of 5,000+ exercises and want to turn raw footage into short, consistent educational reference videos for coach education and client support — today each one takes ~15s in Premiere and we want a repeatable, AI-assisted production pipeline. This task is ONE run of that pipeline on a single representative exercise, the Goblet Squat, so we can validate the repeatable unit before scaling it across the library.

Supplied assets: (1) a raw ~15s 4K landscape clip of a coach demoing the goblet squat; (2) our gym's square logo PNG (dark logo on transparent-ish background); (3) a flat hand-drawn red 'muscle-activation' arrow/callout PNG we use to point at the working muscle groups.

What we need produced this run:
1. REUSABLE WATERMARK — our logo turned into a transparent, corner-sized, white version that reads on dark gym footage (this becomes a reusable overlay asset for the whole library).
2. REUSABLE MUSCLE-GROUP CALLOUT — the hand-drawn arrow cleaned up into a crisp scalable vector recolored to our brand accent, sized as an overlay element (also reusable library-wide).
3. VERTICAL REEL — the raw clip reframed to 1080x1920 vertical (full length, no trimming at this step) and then cut down by AI into a punchy ~15s highlight 'reference reel' of the key reps.

Honesty note for the vendor: we understand the actual frame-by-frame compositing (placing the watermark and arrow onto the video, adding on-screen text, transitions) stays in Premiere on our side — what we want from this automated pipeline is every input asset and the reframed/cut reel prepared and organized so that final Premiere step is fast and identical every time.

Take my mixed-lighting packaging photos, color-grade them into one cohesive polished hero set at a uniform 1920x1080, seat the kraft box on a clean title card, and make a background-removed hero cut-out of the cosmetics jar.
Full brief
I run a small packaging design studio and I'm launching a new website. I have a folder of finished work — six photographs/mockups of packaging projects I've shipped (a tea carton, a cosmetics jar, a coffee bag, a craft-beer can, a perfume box, and a chocolate bar sleeve), all shot in my studio over the past year so they don't match: some are warm, some are cool, a couple are slightly crooked, exposure drifts shot to shot. I also have one clean photo of a plain kraft box I want to use as the title card — please seat it on a clean solid studio card so I have even negative space to overlay my logo.

I want all of this pulled together into a cohesive, polished HERO image set for the top of my homepage — a matched grade across every shot that makes my design work look its absolute best, plus a clean title card and a background-removed hero product cut-out I can drop into the page. Please do the following, in order, so the look is cohesive across every shot:

1) Bring all my supplied photos in and get them straight and uniformly exposed (auto-straighten the crooked ones, auto-tone, lift the dark portions a touch).
2) Give the whole set one consistent grade — neutralize the mixed white balance toward a clean studio look, push vibrance so the print colors pop, apply a single cinematic Lightroom preset across every frame, and add a light film grain so they read as one family.
3) For the title card: seat the kraft box on a solid charcoal studio card so there's clean negative space for my logo, and also make a clean "cut-out" hero variant of the cosmetics jar — remove its background and drop it onto a solid charcoal card.
4) Crop/resize every graded frame to a uniform 1920x1080 so the set is uniform.

Quality bar: every shot must look like it belongs to the same set; print colors must be punchy but not blown out; the title-card plate must be clean with even negative space.

We need you to: (1) stand up an asset workspace; (2) take in our authored templates, our catalog data (catalog_data.csv, ~24 SKUs), our product hero photo (hero_product.jpg) and our logo (logo_master.png); (3) prep the art that flows into the merge — isolate the product from its messy shot, clean the tone, build a clean bleed-safe background by cropping a licensed stock texture to the A4-plus-bleed frame, and vectorize the logo so it stays crisp at any print size; (4) run the data merge into BOTH the catalog .indd (one catalog card per row) and the price-tag .ai (Illustrator Variables, one tag per row); (5) export both as print-ready PDFs (catalog at A4 with bleed, tags at tag size); and (6) hand back the finished print-ready files. All copy is in Tamil and the look must stay clearly traditional — warm, festive, gold/maroon tones, eye-catching from a distance. I will supply you: (1) my authored Illustrator master files for the banners with all Tamil typography already set correctly in licensed Tamil fonts (do NOT re-typeset or translate — typography is locked), (2) one wide hero photograph of my premises/service scene that needs heavy correction and a warm traditional grade, (3) my brand logo as a flat raster file that I need cleaned up into crisp vector for large print, and (4) a low-res PDF proof of last year's banner that I want converted back into an editable layout source.

What I need from you, all on the Adobe production side:

- Convert my old PDF proof into an editable InDesign source so I can reuse last year's layout.
- Hand back a single packaged folder with every final and source file organised.

Full brief
VIDYA PATH CLASSES needs a clean, premium, professional roadside banner (10 ft x 5 ft, 2:1) that stays readable from the road and presents the course/contact info without clutter. The brand palette is primary #046CB8 and secondary #02ADEF, headings/key numbers in bold Inter, with subject-hinting icons, a confident-but-minimal photo of students, and understated geometric elements. The freelancer has already authored the layered banner in InDesign with every line of verbatim copy (institute name, tagline \"Where Learning Meets Success\", the Pre-Foundation / 9th-10th / 11th-12th course list, \"ADMISSIONS OPEN\", the three phone numbers with +91 90000 00000 most prominent, the \"Railway Station Road, Multai\" location, and the four feature bullets). That authored layout (.indd) plus a raw, slightly-tilted DSLR photo of students, a flat icon sheet, and the brand-color swatch file are the client inputs.

Your Adobe production job, end to end:
1. Stand up the project folders and load/preview the raw student photo and the icon sheet.
2. Fix the photo geometry: auto-straighten the tilted horizon, then crop to the banner hero band aspect.
3. Correct and grade it to the brand: auto-tone for a clean baseline, then warm/cool the white balance and push the dominant tones toward the #046CB8 / #02ADEF brand blues via a color overlay and a targeted single-colour saturation lift so the photo \"matches the specs\".

7. Build the \"understated geometric element\": take the brand-blue field and render a halftone/duotone texture in the brand colours for a modern, minimal accent.
8. Export the client-authored InDesign banner layout to the final print-ready, high-resolution CMYK PDF for large-format flex printing.

The client signs off once the PDF opens cleanly, colours match #046CB8/#02ADEF in CMYK, and the text hierarchy is legible at full 10ft x 5ft size.

Full brief
Crumb & Co., a small-batch wholesale bakery, needs its B2B distributor catalog finished for print and PDF hand-out. The owner has already authored an InDesign catalog template (crumbco_catalog_template.pdf) — an 8.5x11 portrait, multi-page grid layout with repeating product cells, each cell holding an image frame plus real InDesign data-merge fields (<<product_name>>, <<sku>>, <<description>>, <<case_pack>>, <<wholesale_price>>) and section headers for Breads, Pastries, Cakes & Slices, and Cookies & Bars, with a masthead frame for the wordmark and a full-bleed cover panel. The owner has also handed off the wholesale product roster as a CSV (12 SKUs across the four sections, each with a keyword-rich product description, case-pack quantity, and B2B wholesale price) and twelve raw product photos shot quickly on the bakery counter — sourdough boules, seeded rye, croissants, cinnamon rolls, a layer cake, brownies, chocolate-chip cookies, and more. The photos are unappetizing as-shot: slightly tilted, flat and dull, cool fluorescent white balance, and cluttered counter backgrounds. The job: (1) make every product photo look like a "high-quality image" — straighten the tilted frames, auto-tone to fix the flat exposure, warm the cool white balance toward a golden bakery look, push vibrance so crust and glaze read appetizing, apply a consistent bakery-warm preset across all twelve so they match, and crop every photo to the identical square (1:1) ratio the template's cells expect; (2) vectorize the flat Crumb & Co. wordmark PNG into a clean SVG so the masthead stays razor-sharp at print size; (3) upload all the prepped assets (twelve graded 1:1 photos, the vector wordmark) to Creative Cloud storage; (4) run the client's authored .indd through an InDesign data-merge against the roster CSV so every product cell binds its name, SKU, description, case pack, and wholesale price, with each graded photo dropping into its matching cell; (5) export the merged catalog to a print-ready ~300 DPI PDF for the print run and a high-resolution JPEG of the cover/spread for emailing to distributors. Deliverable dimensions: US Letter 8.5x11 portrait, print-ready CMYK-quality PDF plus a max-quality JPEG. Brand constraints: keep the warm/golden bakery palette consistent across every photo, the wordmark must stay crisp at masthead scale, and all descriptions/prices bind verbatim from the supplied roster CSV — do not rewrite the copy.

Northgate Dental Students' Congress 2027 is a two-day event bringing roughly 1,000 delegates from dental schools across the country together for speakers, workshops, a gala dinner and socials. Our brand identity is already signed off, and we now need the physical delegate name badges produced from our attendee list — one personalised badge per delegate. We have handed off everything the job needs: our approved event wordmark as a flat high-contrast PNG (northgate_wordmark.png); an authored InDesign badge template (badge_template.pdf) laid out at 90x130mm portrait with 3mm bleed, containing real InDesign Data Merge fields (<<FullName>>, <<School>>, <<Role>>, <<QRPath>>), a placeholder frame for the vectorized wordmark, a full-width role colour-band frame, and a QR image frame; our delegate roster export (delegate_roster.csv) with one row per delegate holding full name, school, role (Delegate / Speaker / Committee / Press) and the matching role-QR filename; and four flat role-band QR marks as PNGs (one per role, each a solid-colour block with the check-in QR). The wordmark PNG is slightly oversized and off-centre for the badge frame and needs cleaning and vectorizing so it stays razor-sharp at print size; the four QR PNGs are inconsistent sizes and must be squared and cropped to the badge's QR frame. Roles, names and schools all come from the roster as-is — nothing is invented; long names must bind into the template's auto-fit name frame without clipping.

Audit Willowfen Press's supplied 32-page KDP picture-book interior .indd, its exported interior PDF, and the wraparound cover PDF against the KDP spec sheet — checking trim, bleed, margins, spine width, image resolution and caption overset — and emit a marked-up preflight report plus proof renders that says whether the files will pass KDP preflight.
Full brief
Willowfen Press is a small independent children's-book publisher about to upload its next paperback, "Pip & the Paper Moon", to Amazon KDP. Our illustrator and layout designer have already built the files, but our last title bounced twice in KDP's preflight (spine width off, one illustration under-resolution, a caption clipped), so before we upload again we want an independent print-QA pass. We are handing off four things: (1) the authored InDesign interior template (pip_interior_template.pdf) — a 32-page 8.5x11 in trim book with real InDesign data-merge caption fields (<<page_no>>, <<caption>>, <<alt_note>>) placed on each illustrated spread; (2) the exported interior PDF our designer produced from it (pip_interior_export.pdf) — note it came in at 33 pages, one more than the 32 the book should be, because a stray front proof/title sheet was left in on export; (3) the wraparound paperback cover our designer built to the KDP cover template (pip_cover_wrap.pdf — front + spine + back on one sheet); and (4) the KDP spec sheet we were given (kdp_spec_sheet.pdf) that states the required trim (8.5x11 in), bleed (0.125 in on outside edges), interior safe margin (0.375 in), minimum image resolution (300 DPI), and the spine-width formula for a 32-page white-paper paperback (~0.0725 in). We also include the filled caption data (pip_captions.csv) that maps to the interior template's merge fields. What we need from you: go through the files and tell us, in writing, whether they will pass KDP preflight the first time. Specifically: pull a proof render of the interior template and of the exported interior PDF so we can compare them page for page; inline-preview a representative illustrated spread and the full cover sheet so bleed, safe-margin and spine placement can be eyeballed; read the KDP spec sheet and pull out the exact required numbers; and re-run the caption data-merge into the authored interior template so any long caption that would overset or clip in a text frame is caught (that was one of last time's failures). Then write up a clean, itemized preflight report — one line per check (trim, bleed, margins, spine width, image resolution, caption overset, font embedding, page count) with a PASS / FLAG verdict and a short note, ending with an overall go / no-go and a punch-list of what to fix before upload. Deliver the written report plus the proof renders you pulled. Do NOT redesign or re-lay-out anything — this is a review, not a rebuild; every caption and price stays as supplied.

Audit every page of the laid-out Lumen Quarterly issue proof against the supplied Lumen brand style guide and return a marked-up, page-referenced brand-consistency findings report listing each colour / logo / typography / imagery drift and the exact rule it breaks.
Full brief
Lumen Quarterly is a fictional independent arts-and-culture magazine published by Lumen House Press. Our in-house junior designer has finished laying out the Autumn 2026 issue in InDesign and exported it as a print proof PDF, but before it goes to the printer we need a fresh set of eyes to check that the whole issue actually stays inside our brand framework — our board is strict about consistency and the last issue went out with an off-palette pull-quote and a stretched masthead lock-up that we only caught in print. You will receive: (1) lumen_autumn2026_proof.pdf, the full 16-page laid-out issue (cover, masthead, contents, editor's letter, three feature spreads, department pages, back-cover ad); (2) lumen_brand_styleguide.pdf, our complete brand style guide covering the approved colour palette (Lumen Ink #1B2A4A, Signal Coral #FF5A47, Paper #F4F1EA — with the exact hex values and the rule that body text is Lumen Ink only), the masthead / logo lock-up rules (clear-space, minimum size, never stretched or recoloured), the typography system (Freight Display for headlines, Untitled Sans for body, specified sizes and tracking), and the imagery tone rules (warm, editorial, consistent grade; no cold or oversaturated photos); and (3) two flat reference images — the approved palette swatch strip and the correct masthead lock-up — to compare on-page elements against. The job is an audit, not a redesign — do NOT re-lay-out, restyle, recolour or edit anything. Go through every page, compare what is on the page against the guideline, and hand back a brand-consistency audit report that, for each issue found, gives the page number, the on-page region, a plain-language description of the drift, the specific guideline clause it violates, the approved value versus the observed value, and a severity (blocker / warning / nit). We expect you to catch things like: a headline set in the wrong weight or the wrong face, a coral used at the wrong hex, the masthead placed with too little clear-space or subtly stretched, a feature photo that reads cold/blue against the warm-editorial imagery rule, and body copy set in a non-approved colour. Deliver the findings as a clean marked-up report file plus the raw findings as a structured data file, and open with a one-page cover summary giving the total count by severity. Page size is A4 portrait; the report is for the editor and the board, not the printer.

AO-85 Ironclad parts catalog pre-press audit: merge-proof render, spec-row extraction + CSV cross-check, overset/missing-field findings report
Layout & Data Manufacturing Industrial 13 calls 3 outputs 14 checks · 9a/5e ▼
Render our authored InDesign parts-catalog template against the master parts CSV into a proof, then audit it page by page — read back every printed spec row, cross-check it against the source data, and hand back a findings report calling out overset/clipped part numbers, blank spec cells, and a section-count imbalance across the five sections before we send ~100 pages to print.
Full brief
Ironclad Elevator & Electrical Supply is a wholesale distributor of electrical and elevator replacement parts selling to service technicians, maintenance supervisors, and electrical contractors. Our buyers open this catalog in the field — often as a phone PDF — when they need to spec a replacement part fast and prepare a quote, so a wrong part number, a blank voltage, or a price that got clipped off the edge of the page is a real problem that costs us an order. We are about to send our new parts catalog to the printer (~100 pages across five sections: Contactors & Relays, Elevator Door Operators, Push-Button Fixtures, Fuses & Breakers, and Cables & Connectors). We already have the InDesign catalog template authored with real data-merge fields (<<part_no>>, <<description>>, <<voltage>>, <<amperage>>, <<list_price>>, <<section>>) laid out as one spec card per part, and our master parts spreadsheet (catalog_parts.csv, ~181 SKUs). Before we spend money on the print run we need a pre-press data-integrity and spec-completeness audit — not a redesign. Specifically: (1) run our authored template through the data merge against the CSV and export a proof PDF so we can see exactly what will print; (2) convert/inspect that proof page by page and read back what actually rendered on each card; (3) extract the printed spec rows and cross-check them against the source CSV to catch part numbers that ran overset (long codes clipped by the frame), any blank/empty voltage-amperage-price cells that would leave a technician guessing, and any section-count imbalance across the five sections (a section carrying a different number of SKUs than the others, tallied from the CSV and confirmed on the proof); and (4) deliver a written findings report — a table listing every flagged part number, its page, the field at fault, the CSV value vs. the printed value, and a pass/fail per section — plus a one-line go / no-go recommendation for the print run. Page size is US Letter portrait; keep our section order. Deliver the findings report table and the report summary.

Full brief
Amberleaf Tea Studio, a small independent tea-branding consultancy, is prepping two of its house tea brands for a production run and needs the artwork made print-ready. The studio has already generated the concept artwork with an AI image tool but only has flat raster PNGs: a wordmark lockup for 'Golden Chai Co.' (warm amber-and-cream with a subtle gold gradient), a wordmark lockup for 'Silverleaf Green' (cool sage-green with a fine leaf glyph), and one ornamental 'crest' mark (a symmetrical scrollwork badge with a small tea-leaf motif meant to sit on both brands' packaging). All three rasters have the usual AI-export problems: soft anti-aliased edges, a faint off-white textured card behind the art, mild luminance noise, and each is tilted a couple of degrees off level. None of these can go to a printer as-is because they do not scale and have no transparency. The studio also supplies a flat mockup image of a blank stand-up coffee/tea pouch it wants to use as the packaging shape. The job: (1) ingest all three raster logos and get clean working copies; auto-straighten each tilted mark and tonally clean it so edges are true and the near-white card is even; (2) crop each mark tight to its true artwork bounds and knock the background to transparent so the trace has no halo; (3) VECTORIZE each cleaned mark into a crisp, fully-scalable SVG master while preserving every colour and the gold gradient exactly as in the concept — these three SVGs are the primary editable/print-ready vector deliverables (AI/EPS/PDF are the same master exported to those formats); (4) from the ornamental crest, derive a single-color / knockout vector (crest silhouette solid-filled) for one-colour foil, embossing and small favicon use, and a halftone 'print-screen' treatment for merch and kraft-paper packaging; (5) produce the 'matching front-facing product label' the brief asks for: crop the supplied stand-up-pouch mockup to just its flat front panel and lay a clean solid kraft-tone base band on that panel, delivering the print-ready front-label base panel that fits the new vector style — the cleaned Golden Chai wordmark + crest are dropped onto it by the studio in the layered vector files. Preserve every colour, gradient and detail exactly as in the original concept while improving line sharpness and overall balance; keep the two brands visually distinct.

AO-87 Little Lighthouse charity tee: rebuild two raster concept mockups into clean 3-spot-color screen-print separations (front chest + full back) as print-ready vector
Vector & Print Fashion Apparel 35 calls 9 outputs 14 checks · 5a/9e ▼
Rebuild the client's two flat raster tee concepts (front chest + full back) into clean, production-ready screen-print separations: isolate each of the 3 approved brand spot colors and force it to its exact PANTONE hex as a solid flat plate, vectorize every color layer, and export per-color separation vectors plus a combined proof PDF.
Full brief
Little Lighthouse Fund, a children's charity, is running a fundraising T-shirt campaign and needs its two established concepts turned into production-ready screen-print artwork. The design lead has handed off two flat, high-contrast raster concept mockups exported from their design tool — a front-chest lockup (a stylized lighthouse-and-wave badge with the words LITTLE LIGHTHOUSE) and a full-back design (a larger lighthouse scene with a supporter tagline) — plus a one-page brand-guidelines PDF that pins the campaign palette to exactly three approved spot colors: Beacon Red (PANTONE 186 C, hex #C8102E), Harbor Navy (PANTONE 2758 C, hex #1B2A5B), and Sand Cream (PANTONE 7401 C, hex #F0E6C8). The printer's constraints are strict and non-negotiable: MAXIMUM 3 spot colors per shirt, NO gradients, NO halftones, all lettering already flattened into the raster (no live fonts needed), and each color must sit on its own clean, solid separation so it can be burned to a screen. Front chest prints ~10cm wide, full back ~30cm wide. Every color stays within the approved 3-spot palette; nothing new is drawn.

Vector & Print Sports & Recreation 22 calls 5 outputs 14 checks · 6a/8e ▼
Clean up the club's phone photo of a stitched sample crest, vectorize the emblem into razor-sharp scalable art at 3-6 inch patch size, reduce it to flat spot-color separations, and hand back a factory-ready SVG plus exported vector masters.
Full brief
Ridgeline Rovers FC, an amateur mountain-town football (soccer) club, is ordering embroidered crest patches and sleeve badges from a factory and needs its emblem turned into proper production-ready vector artwork first. The only artwork the club has is a phone photo of a sample patch that a previous designer stitched off an early draft (crest_sample_patch.jpg) — a shield-shaped crest with a stylized mountain-ridge silhouette, a football, the letters "RRFC", and the founding year "EST. 2014" on a banner ribbon, stitched in four thread colors (forest green, cream, slate grey, black outline) on a heathered fabric backing. The photo is a real hand-held shot: tilted about 3 degrees, dull and slightly underexposed, a cool/green color cast from the fabric, and the twill weave texture shows across every color so the edges look fuzzy. That texture and cast make it useless for a factory as-is.

The job: (1) clean the reference so it can be traced — deskew it level, auto-tone to fix the flat exposure, neutralize the green fabric cast so the four thread colors read true, then push contrast hard to crush the woven-fabric texture and drive every element toward a clean, flat, high-contrast silhouette; knock the heathered backing to transparent so the trace has no halo. (2) VECTORIZE the cleaned crest into a clean, scalable SVG — this is the master emblem, and it must stay razor-sharp when the factory scales it to the requested medium 3-6 inch patch size. (3) Because embroidery and woven patches need each color as one flat solid thread, reduce the emblem to FLAT SPOT SEPARATIONS: go element by element, select each color region, and lock it to a single solid ink from the club's 4-color palette (no gradients, no anti-aliased blends), then pull a single-color BLACK OUTLINE plate the factory uses for the merrowed-border stitch path, and re-vectorize the flattened art. (4) Deliver a one-color KNOCKOUT (solid emblem silhouette) the factory can use to cut the twill/felt backing. (5) Export the artwork to vector masters (PDF/PNG/SVG) from a genuine authored .ai so the club and factory have the emblem in every format the press needs before the run.

Palette: forest green #2E5A3A, cream #F2E9D0, slate grey #6B7078, black #111111 outline. Deliverables: master crest SVG, flat spot-separated SVG, black-outline plate, one-color knockout, and exported vector masters. Stitch digitizing (.dst/.pes) is handled by the factory from these vector masters — it is not part of this hand-off.

Clean and vectorize LUMIÈRE MÉNAGE's supplied flat monochrome logo concept into an editable SVG master, then assemble the full reversible variant system — black-on-white master, white-on-dark knockout, avatar/PFP crop, stacked lockup, one-color black print PNG, a mono-tint alt, a monochrome palette recipe, and a font recommendation — all scalable from avatar to signage.
Full brief
LUMIÈRE MÉNAGE is a fictional modern clean-beauty and skincare label preparing to launch across social, e-commerce, unit cartons, and large in-store signage. After an internal round we have approved ONE monochrome logo concept and now need it PRODUCTIONIZED into a fully editable, reversible brand-mark system — this is a finishing/assembly job, not a from-scratch design round.

We supply a single flat, high-contrast raster export of the approved concept: a crisp geometric monogram ("LM" resolved into an abstract, symmetric negative-space shape) sitting above the wordmark "LUMIÈRE MÉNAGE" set in a clean modern condensed sans, rendered pure black on a near-white background, no gradients, no illustration, no flourishes. The concept scan is slightly skewed and the background is an off-white (#F5F5F3), not true white.

Deliverables, all chained in the Adobe connector:
1) Ingest our supplied concept PNG and get a clean working copy — straighten the slight skew and auto-tone so the black is dense and the edges are true.
2) Knock the off-white background out to true transparency so the trace has no halo/fringe.
3) Vectorize the cleaned lockup into a clean, fully editable SVG — this is the MASTER vector (basis for the requested AI/SVG editable file + high-res PNG exports).
4) Produce the REVERSED knockout: a white-on-dark version of the mark that reads perfectly when reversed out on dark packaging and signage (the brief's key requirement).
5) Derive a tight AVATAR / social-PFP version from the monogram alone (square, centered) that stays recognizable at avatar size.
6) Build a STACKED lockup crop for narrow / vertical placements.
7) Produce a ONE-COLOR pure-black print PNG (for single-color foil/deboss and small-format print).
8) Produce a single MONOCHROMATIC brand-tint alt (one hue only — no multicolor, honoring "clean monochrome palette") for tonal applications.
9) Recommend a brand font family + heading/supporting pairing that matches the modern condensed wordmark tone.
10) Emit a MONOCHROME palette recipe (black / dark grey / off-white / paper hex callouts) as the color-palette deliverable.

Hard constraints (honor the brief AND connector ground truth): stay strictly monochrome — no gradients, no multicolor, no vintage/distress treatment. Everything must reverse cleanly, scale from a social-media avatar up to large signage, and arrive as an editable vector plus high-res PNGs. No from-scratch logo drawing, no generative fill, no AI object removal, no compositing — the supplied concept is the single source of truth and every deliverable is derived from it by chaining. The requested AI/EPS export and the printed spec sheet are human/format-export finishing items layered on top of the connector-produced SVG + PNG masters.

Clean and de-skew Apexguard's three AI-drafted PPF/tint logo rasters, trace them into crisp production SVG masters, derive one-color knockouts for vinyl weeding, then assemble a multi-size die-cut vinyl decal/sticker sheet by binding the vector marks and the approved-sizes CSV into the client's authored cut-line template and exporting a press-ready PDF + SVG.
Full brief
Apexguard Auto Film, a fictional performance-automotive brand selling paint protection film (PPF) and window tint, is rebranding and needs its new identity turned into production-ready vector artwork and a print-ready vinyl decal sheet for its shop glass, product boxes, and installer-kit labels. The client has drafted the concepts with an AI image tool and only has flat raster PNGs: a master wordmark lockup for 'Apexguard' (a clean modern condensed sans in matte black with a single deep-blue accent chevron, premium/minimalist, no gradients), a sub-brand mark for 'Apexguard SHIELD' (the PPF line — the wordmark plus a simple hex-shield glyph), and a sub-brand mark for 'Apexguard TINT' (the window-tint line — the wordmark plus a tint-bar glyph rendered as flat bands). All three rasters carry the usual AI-export problems: soft anti-aliased edges, a faint off-white textured card behind the art, mild luminance noise, and each is tilted a couple of degrees off level. They cannot go to a vinyl cutter/printer as-is because they do not scale, have no clean cut path, and have no transparency. The client also supplies (a) an authored die-cut decal-sheet template (decal_sheet_template.ai) laid out on a single sheet with several registered sticker cells at different sizes — small installer-kit labels up to a large window/glass piece — each cell carrying a real placement/merge field plus a registered cut-line and bleed, and (b) a CSV of the approved sticker sizes and cell labels (cell_label, size_in, which_mark, mark) that matches the template's merge fields.

The job: (1) ingest the three raster logos and get clean working copies; auto-straighten each tilted mark and tonally clean it so the black is true, the blue accent is crisp, and the near-white card is even; (2) crop each mark tight to its true artwork bounds and knock the background to transparent so the trace has no halo; (3) VECTORIZE each cleaned mark into a crisp, fully-scalable SVG master preserving the exact black + deep-blue palette — these three SVGs are the primary editable/print-ready vector deliverables (AI/EPS are the same master exported to those formats); (4) from the master wordmark, derive a single-color / knockout vector (solid-fill silhouette) for one-color window vinyl, etched glass and weeding-friendly cutter output, plus a white-on-dark knockout for dark boxes and tinted glass; (5) ASSEMBLE the multi-size vinyl decal/sticker sheet the briefs ask for: upload the cleaned vector marks, then run the client's authored decal_sheet_template.ai through a vector data-merge against the approved-sizes CSV so each registered cell is populated with the correct mark at the correct size behind its cut-line and bleed, and export the assembled sheet to a press-ready PDF and a production SVG; (6) recommend a brand-safe font pairing that matches the wordmark so the client can extend the identity across packaging and web. Keep it premium, minimalist and confident — no gradients on the master, no mascots, no vintage badges — and preserve the black + deep-blue palette exactly. Sizes and cell labels stay exactly as given in the CSV.

AO-91 Maison Valcere jewelry house: vector & print-readiness audit of the supplied luxury wordmark pack against the brand guideline and press spec (marked-up findings report)
Vector & Print Jewelry Luxury Goods 14 calls 2 outputs 16 checks · 5a/11e ▼
Audit the supplied Maison Valcere luxury wordmark pack (master SVG + raster export) against the brand guideline and the press/foil spec, and return a marked-up, region-referenced vector & print-readiness findings report listing every hairline-stroke, line-weight, palette, kerning and non-print-ready-path defect and the exact rule it breaks.
Full brief
Maison Valcere is a fictional independent high-jewelry house (fine rings, pendants and bespoke pieces) that has just received its finished logo pack from an outside brand studio and, before it goes onto embossed presentation boxes, foil-stamped certificates, the e-commerce header and the video title cards, wants an independent set of eyes to confirm the mark is genuinely production-clean. The identity is meant to feel unmistakably premium — a deep-black canvas with crisp white typography, minimal ornamentation, purely typographic with no symbols or icons — and the house is strict that every asset stays consistent across packaging, print and screen. You are handed four things: (1) valcere_wordmark_master.svg, the "production" vector master the studio delivered; (2) valcere_wordmark_web.png, the flat raster export the house has been using online; (3) valcere_brand_guideline.pdf, the guideline stating the monochrome palette (Valcere Noir #0E0E10, Champagne #E8DCC2, Blanc #FAF8F3 — with the rule that the wordmark is "purely typographic, no symbols or icons, never recoloured outside the monochrome palette, minimum print width 22mm, minimum hairline stroke 0.35pt / 1.5px at favicon size"); and (4) valcere_press_spec.pdf, the printer/foil spec sheet (foil-stamp minimum stroke, CMYK/spot conversion requirement, "all strokes must be expanded to filled paths, no open contours, no RGB-only fills"). The job is an AUDIT, not a redraw — do NOT re-letter, re-trace, recolour or fix anything, and do NOT deliver a new logo. Go through the mark region by region and compare what the pack actually contains against the guideline and the press spec, then hand back a vector & print-readiness audit report that, for each issue, gives the mark region (which glyph / stroke / variant), a plain-language description of the defect, the specific guideline or press-spec clause it violates, the approved value vs. the observed value, and a severity (blocker / warning / nit). We expect you to catch things like: a hairline serif or connecting stroke thinner than the 0.35pt foil-stamp minimum that will drop out when stamped or shrunk to a favicon; a stray decorative anchor / tiny symbol that violates the "purely typography, no symbols" rule; the reverse (knockout) variant sitting on an off-palette near-black instead of Valcere Noir #0E0E10; kerning drift where the raster web export does not match the vector master's letter-spacing; and paths in the master SVG that are not print-ready (unexpanded strokes, open contours, RGB fills that were never converted for spot/foil). Deliver the report as a clean A4 portrait PDF plus the raw findings as a structured file, and include a one-page cover summary with the total count by severity and a go / no-go-for-press verdict. The report is for the house's creative director and the printer, not a redesign.

AO-92 Wandergrain Supply screen-print pre-flight: audit 4 supplied traveller tee vectors for separation-readiness, registration & spot-color count, emit a marked-up seps report + print-shop go/no-go note
Vector & Print Fashion Apparel 20 calls 4 outputs 16 checks · 4a/12e ▼
Pre-flight four supplied traveller-themed t-shirt vector graphics for screen-print separation readiness -- verify transparent backgrounds, count distinct spot colors per design, check for registration marks and thin-line survivability, vectorize/inspect to flag raster contamination -- and emit a marked-up per-design seps audit report with a go/no-go recommendation for the exposure room.
Full brief
Wandergrain Supply Co., a small-batch apparel screen-print shop, has just received four traveller-themed t-shirt graphics from a freelance designer for its new "Modern Wanderer" tee line (universal travel icons -- a passport-stamp badge, a latitude/longitude coordinate mark, a minimalist skyline, and a compass-rose crest). Before any of these hit the exposure room and burn screens, the shop needs an independent pre-flight / separation audit -- the designer swears the files are "pre-flighted for screen print," but the shop has been burned before by art that looked fine on screen and fell apart on the press. We are NOT redesigning anything and NOT producing final films; we need an honest QA report. For each of the four designs, please verify and document: (1) background integrity -- the art must sit on a genuinely transparent background with no stray off-white halo or leftover matte that would print as a phantom screen; (2) spot-color / ink count -- count the distinct flat spot colors in each design and flag any design that exceeds our 4-color manual-press limit, or that hides near-duplicate colors that should be merged to one screen; (3) registration & trap readiness -- check whether the art carries registration marks / crop guides and whether abutting colors are cleanly separable or will need a choke/trap note; (4) detail survivability -- flag any hairline strokes, tiny text, or fine detail below what a 156-mesh screen can hold, and confirm the "keep text editable" promise by checking whether type is still crisp vector or has been flattened to messy raster; (5) vector cleanliness -- confirm each design is truly vector (not a raster PNG masquerading as art) by test-vectorizing and comparing. Deliverables: a per-design marked-up preview of each graphic (so we can circle problems), plus a single written seps pre-flight report (a recipe/findings note) that lists, per design, the spot-color count, pass/fail on transparency, registration presence, minimum-detail concern, and a clear GO / FIX-FIRST / NO-GO verdict the exposure room can act on. Files supplied as an Illustrator-exported package: four graphics (three already flattened to PNG with transparency, one still a layered vector) plus the designer's own color-spec sheet. Keep everything spot-color / vector oriented -- no CMYK conversions, no re-coloring, no new artwork.

AO-93 Torqex Industrial nameplate logo pack: print-readiness preflight audit of the supplied vector artwork (open paths, RGB, un-outlined text, stray points) into a marked-up findings report
Vector & Print Manufacturing Industrial 17 calls 2 outputs 15 checks · 5a/10e ▼
Preflight-audit the supplied Torqex vector logo pack (.ai/.eps master, SVG, PDF, plus one-colour and reverse variants) against the manufacturer's nameplate print spec and return a marked-up, file-and-region-referenced findings report listing every open path, RGB colour, un-outlined text run, stray point, hairline stroke and background/bleed defect with the exact rule it breaks and a severity.
Full brief
Torqex Industrial is a fictional maker of hydraulic torque tools and machinery, and we are about to send our brand mark out to a nameplate vendor to be laser-etched onto anodized-aluminium equipment plates and screen-printed onto tool cases. A previous contractor delivered our 'Torqex' logo as a vector pack, but before it goes to the etching/print house we need a fresh set of eyes to confirm the artwork is genuinely production-ready — the last vendor rejected a batch because a logo file had live text and an RGB blue that shifted on the plate, and we cannot afford another rejected run. This is an AUDIT, not a redesign: do NOT redraw, restyle, re-colour or re-letter anything. You will receive two things. (1) torqex_logo_pack: the delivered artwork — torqex_master.ai (the editable vector master), torqex_master.eps and torqex_master.pdf (the same mark exported), torqex_logo.svg (the web export), plus torqex_onecolour_black.ai (single-colour knockout) and torqex_reverse_white.ai (reverse/knockout-on-dark variant). (2) torqex_nameplate_print_spec.pdf, the vendor's print-spec sheet stating the rules the pack must satisfy: all colours must be CMYK (or spot) — no RGB; the approved brand colour is Torqex Blue at C100 M72 K18 (do NOT ship RGB #1B49E5); all text must be converted to outlines (no live fonts); paths must be closed with no stray/open anchor points; the minimum printable stroke weight for laser etching is 0.25 pt (0.09 mm) — anything thinner drops out; the mark must sit on a transparent background with a 3 mm bleed on the placed variants; the one-colour and reverse variants must be a single flat colour with no gradients or tints. Go through every file, compare what is actually in the artwork against the spec, and hand back a print-readiness preflight report that, for each issue found, gives the file name, the region / element on the mark, a plain-language description of the defect, the specific spec clause it violates, the observed value vs the approved value, and a severity (blocker / warning / nit). We expect you to catch things like: the SVG and the .pdf export carrying RGB colour instead of CMYK; the tagline text in the master left as live (un-outlined) fonts; a couple of stray/duplicate anchor points and one un-closed path on the icon; a hairline register line under 0.25 pt that will drop out on the plate; the reverse variant accidentally carrying a faint gradient instead of a flat white; and one variant exported on a solid white background instead of transparent with no bleed. Some files are clean and compliant so the audit has to distinguish good from bad, not just flag everything. Deliver the report as a clean A4 PDF plus the raw findings as a structured file, with a one-page cover summary giving the total count by severity. The report is for our production manager and the nameplate vendor, not a design revision.

Take Vitalé Labs' raw wellness talking-head footage (a primary take plus five supplemental coverage clips), auto-cut it into a punchy highlight sizzle at a target duration, then export platform-ready ~18s Reel, ~18s Short and 1:1 feed versions plus a hook-and-hashtag post-caption note.
Full brief
Vitalé Labs is a direct-to-consumer wellness and DNA-supplement brand that publishes short educational clips explaining how personalized nutrition works. We just filmed our lead nutrition scientist, Dr. Nadia Reuter, explaining our new "GenoBalance" DNA supplement panel — a primary talking-head take plus five short supplemental coverage clips from other angles, about ~55s of raw 1920x1080 landscape footage in total, shot on a mirrorless camera. It is rough material: she rambles, restarts a couple of sentences, and there are long pauses while she checks her notes, shot in a plain untreated office. We need this turned into ONE tight, premium, trustworthy sizzle Reel — clean and modern and educational, NOT flashy or meme-style. Deliverables and specs: (1) cut the rambling footage down to a punchy ~18s highlight version that keeps the strongest, most watchable moments and drops the dead air — keep viewers glued from the first second; (2) from that finished cut, export three platform-ready versions at the correct dimensions with no stretching: a 9:16 vertical Instagram Reel (1080x1920), a 9:16 vertical YouTube Short (1080x1920), and a 1:1 square feed post (1080x1080); (3) also hand back a plain-text post-caption note — the 3-second hook line and hashtag set from our attached script — that our team will paste into each platform's post caption. Keep the brand feel restrained and professional per our kit. Attached: the raw take plus five supplemental coverage clips, a one-page paper-edit / hook script marking the lines we care about, and our brand kit.

AO-95 Voltcast tech-channel delivery QC: audit the outsourced editor's YouTube master + vertical cut against the channel delivery-spec sheet (timecode-referenced video findings report)
Motion & Audio Music, Film, Publishing & Media 14 calls 2 outputs 14 checks · 5a/9e ▼
Audit the outsourced editor's Voltcast episode deliverables -- the 16:9 YouTube master and the 9:16 vertical cut -- against the channel's written delivery-spec sheet, and return a timestamp-referenced QC findings report (as a report PDF plus structured JSON) listing every spec drift: duration, resolution/fps, missing intro/outro, unsafe-margin overlays and off-brand text.
Full brief
Voltcast is a fictional independent consumer-tech review channel run by Voltcast Media that publishes several times a week -- long-form reviews plus short vertical cuts for Shorts / Reels / TikTok. We outsource the actual editing to a rotating pool of junior editors, and before an episode goes live we run a delivery QC pass so nothing off-spec reaches the feed (the last episode published with the price-callout overlay clipped off the bottom on mobile, and we only caught it after it went out).

For this episode ('Voltcast E42 -- Budget Phone Shootout') you will receive four things: (1) voltcast_e42_master_16x9.mp4, the finished 4K 16:9 YouTube master the editor delivered; (2) voltcast_e42_vertical_9x16.mp4, the reformatted vertical Shorts/Reels cut derived from the same edit; (3) voltcast_delivery_spec.pdf, our written channel delivery-spec sheet; and (4) voltcast_brand_frames.png, a reference sheet of our correct intro end-card, lower-third, and price-callout overlay so you can compare on-screen text against the approved look. The delivery-spec sheet states the exact rules: long-form runtime must land in the 8:00-12:00 window; master must be 3840x2160 at 23.976 or 24 fps, H.264; the branded intro end-card must appear in the first 8 seconds and the subscribe/outro card in the final 15 seconds; every text overlay (lower-thirds, spec/price callouts) must sit inside the title-safe margin (5% inset) so it is not clipped, and the vertical 9:16 cut must keep those callouts inside the tighter mobile safe area; on-brand text must use the channel's approved lower-third style, not a default editor font.

The job is an audit, not a re-edit -- do NOT re-cut, re-grade, or re-export the episode. Watch/inspect both deliverables, compare what is actually there against the spec sheet, and hand back a delivery-QC report that, for each issue found, gives the affected file, the timecode (or time range), a plain-language description of the drift, the exact spec clause it violates, the observed-vs-required value, and a severity (blocker / warning / nit). We expect you to catch things like: a runtime that overshoots the 12:00 ceiling, a price-callout overlay that sits too close to the bottom edge on the 16:9 master, a price-callout overlay clipped outside the mobile safe area on the vertical cut, an outro card that is missing or too short, and a lower-third set in the wrong font. Deliver the report as a clean A4 report PDF plus the raw findings as a structured JSON file, and open the PDF with a one-page cover summary counting findings by severity. The report is for our managing editor, not the printer -- it is the go / no-go checklist before we schedule the upload.
Deliverables (2)
Voltcast_E42_Delivery_QC.pdfvoltcast_e42_qc_findings.json
