AO-96 SentinelMesh AI cybersecurity SaaS product video: brand-graded demo cut with 30s promo + 15s teaser cutdowns and on-brand callout / end-card graphic plates
Motion & Audio Tech Software Saas 16 calls 9 outputs 15 checks · 9a/6e ▼
Turn SentinelMesh's raw screen recordings, product b-roll, logo, and brand color reference into a polished ~15s AI-cybersecurity SaaS demo cut plus a ~30s promo cutdown and 15s teaser (with a vertical social reframe), and build on-brand lower-third / call-out / graded end-card graphic plates and a vector logo as the editable-asset set for the Premiere handoff.
Full brief
SentinelMesh is a B2B AI-powered cybersecurity platform that helps organizations reduce human cyber risk through real-time protection, adaptive phishing simulations, and in-the-moment learning nudges. We're preparing our next funding round and a website refresh, and we need a polished marketing and product-demonstration video plus social cutdowns. The finished pieces will run on our website hero, in sales decks, webinars, investor discussions, and across LinkedIn / X. We already have a strong foundation of material and want an editor to turn it into a professional, modern B2B SaaS product video (product footage + motion graphics + animated callouts + captions and visual storytelling — NOT a cartoon-style explainer).

Source material we're supplying: (1) two 1080p screen-capture recordings of the SentinelMesh console — the real-time threat dashboard and the adaptive-simulation builder; (2) a short b-roll clip of the product running on a laptop in a modern office; (3) our logo as a flat PNG; (4) a neutral, ungraded end-card hero still with negative space for a logo lockup; (5) a single brand color-reference frame representing the cool, confident, dark-mode look we want the piece graded toward; and (6) a messaging / talking-points CSV distilled from our whitepapers and website copy (the key claims, in priority order).

We need the freelancer to handle the full edit plus the supporting graphics, mapped to Adobe Creative Cloud connector tools with every step honestly tagged for execution mode:

A. VIDEO — (1) summarize the raw recordings + b-roll so we agree on the key talking points and a logical flow before cutting; (2) produce the primary deliverable: one polished ~15s product-demo cut that surfaces the priority messaging; (3) produce a 30-second promotional cutdown and a 15-second teaser, each as its own tighter pass (repurposed from the same footage, not exact-timestamp trims); (4) reframe the 15-second teaser to a 9:16 vertical version for social, same length (no trimming).

B. BRAND END-CARD + LOOK — from the neutral end-card hero still, build the graded end-card the video closes on and that also locks the brand look the editor matches the master grade to: straighten, auto-tone baseline, push the cool dark-mode color temperature toward the brand reference, shape vibrance/saturation, and crop/resize clean to 1920x1080.

C. GRAPHIC PLATES (standalone PNG / SVG swatch-and-position references, NOT composited onto the video) — the on-brand overlay references the editor rebuilds/lays onto the timeline: (1) vectorize the logo to a clean SVG for the end-card and corner bug; (2) a lower-third bar plate — a solid brand-color bar produced by selecting a region on the end-card canvas and solid-filling it (an opaque swatch/position reference, not a transparent cutout); (3) a call-out badge plate built the same way for on-screen fact call-outs; (4) an on-brand end-card variant with a subtle brand color overlay for the social teaser close.

Deliverables on approval: one ~15s 1080p H.264 master demo; a ~15s promo cutdown and a 15s teaser; a 9:16 vertical reframe of the teaser; one graded 1920x1080 end-card frame; logo SVG; lower-third and call-out PNG plates; and a social end-card variant, together forming the editable-asset set for the Premiere project handoff. Two rounds of feedback should be plenty.

AO-97 Pulsevault club-night recap: assemble a ~15s high-energy sizzle reel from supplied raw footage, graded cover frame + vector logo lockup
Motion & Audio Events & Entertainment 25 calls 4 outputs 14 checks · 5a/9e ▼
Take our raw club-night phone clips plus a hero cover still and venue logo, and assemble a post-ready ~15s high-energy recap: an AI sizzle cut reframed to 1080x1920, an event-info caption sheet, and a fully color-graded cover frame with a crisp vector logo lockup.
Full brief
Pulsevault is a downtown nightclub, and we run a themed event every Friday. We need a punchy recap of last weekend to post on Instagram Reels and TikTok to promote the next one — high-energy, fast-paced, and capturing the vibrant atmosphere of the room. We already have all the raw material; we just need it cut together and finished properly. Here is what we're handing off: (a) three raw vertical clips shot on a phone from the DJ booth and the floor (crowd hands-up, laser/haze sweep, and a confetti drop), all a bit dark and mixed-lit with the club's colored wash; (b) one hero still grabbed from the footage that we want turned into the cover/thumbnail frame; (c) our venue wordmark logo as a flat PNG; and (d) an event-info sheet (next date, doors, ticket link, hashtag) as data for the on-screen captions. Deliverables: 1x final ~15s MP4 ready to post on Instagram and TikTok (Full HD); an on-screen captions/event-info asset; and an exported, fully color-graded 1080x1920 cover frame with our logo locked up in the corner as a crisp vector so it stays sharp. Keep the look on-brand: deep club darkness, punchy neon magenta/cyan pop, energetic. Source assets should stay in our Creative Cloud folder so tweaks are easy each week. NOTE up front: frame-accurate cuts, hard transitions, and animated motion graphics are a manual Premiere/After Effects finish and are out of scope for the automated connector pass — the automated pass delivers the AI sizzle assembly, the ~15s reframe, the captions asset, and the graded cover frame; our editor does the final timeline polish on top.

AO-98 Velvet Hour Sessions live-set footage review: multi-clip raw-concert audit, best-take selection + unusable-clip cull, delivered as a shot-selection log with a flagged-frame contact-sheet PDF
Motion & Audio Arts, Culture & Music 13 calls 3 outputs 14 checks · 4a/10e ▼
Review every raw concert clip from the Velvet Hour Sessions multi-cam shoot, judge keepers vs unusable takes, and deliver a structured shot-selection log (per-clip verdict, reason, best usable stretch, usability rating, coverage tag) plus a contact-sheet PDF of the flagged best-take frames.
Full brief
Velvet Hour Sessions is a fictional intimate live-music night run by the Velvet Hour Room, a small arts-and-culture venue that films one acoustic set a month for its social channels (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube). Last Thursday we filmed the singer-songwriter 'Marlowe Fenn' doing a four-song stripped-back set on three cameras — a locked wide, a roaming handheld, and a close-up on the guitar/hands — and the card dump gave us a folder of a dozen-ish raw clips of very mixed quality. Before our editor builds the actual cut we need a fresh, disciplined pair of eyes to do the footage-review pass first: watch every raw clip end to end, decide which takes are genuinely usable and which are junk, and hand us back a selection log we can build the timeline from. Do NOT cut, grade, add music, or produce a finished video — this is a review-and-select job, exactly the first stage of the edit. You will receive: (1) velvet_hour_raw_clips (the folder of raw concert clips — some are clean keepers, several are unusable: one badly out of focus during the second song, one with a big camera bump / lens smack, one that's mostly dead air and tuning chatter before the song starts, one near-duplicate of a better wide take, and one where the handheld drifts off the performer for half the clip), (2) shoot_notes.csv (the runner's rough log: camera, rough song, and a one-line note per clip like 'wide, song 2, soft?' or 'handheld, song 4, drifts'), and (3) velvet_hour_brand_note.pdf (a short one-pager on what the venue's social edits are for and the 'clean, coherent, story-first, no gimmicks' house style so your keep/cut calls match how the footage will actually be used). Go through each clip against the notes and against what you actually see and hear, and return a shot-selection log that, for every clip, gives: the clip name, which camera/song it is, a KEEP / MAYBE / REJECT verdict, a plain-language reason (what's good or what's wrong — soft focus, camera bump, dead air, drift, redundant, clean), a usability rating (1-5), a note on the strongest usable stretch of the clip described in words (e.g. 'best from the first chorus onward, once focus settles'), and a coverage tag (wide / handheld / close-up) so we can see we have each angle for each song. Finish with a short summary: total clips, how many KEEP vs MAYBE vs REJECT, any song or angle where we're now short on usable coverage, and a one-line recommendation on whether we have enough to build the cut or need a re-shoot of anything. Deliver the log as a clean readable PDF plus the raw findings as a structured data file, and include a contact-sheet PDF showing one representative frame from each KEEP/MAYBE clip (with the clip name under each) so the director can eyeball the selects at a glance. A4 / letter is fine; this is for the director, not for broadcast.

Lunara Silver is a growing D2C brand of handcrafted sterling-silver jewellery. AO-104 Northwind Advisory corporate headshots: batch retouch + grade a 3-frame studio session into LinkedIn/website/print deliverables with clean black-and-white alternates
Photo & Image Professional Services 40 calls 18 outputs 15 checks · 6a/9e ▼
Batch-retouch and colour-grade three raw studio headshot frames of one Northwind executive into a consistent set of fully-finished colour portraits, then produce clean black-and-white alternates and the LinkedIn / website / print-ready crops, delivered as a consistent print/web-ready set.
Full brief
Hi — this is Priya Venkataraman, office manager at Northwind Advisory Partners (a boutique wealth-advisory firm). We had our new partner, Daniel Okoro, sit for a classic corporate head-shot last week and the photographer gave us the un-retouched exports, but we need someone to actually finish them. Please work only from the files I'm attaching: three high-res studio frames of Daniel against our neutral light-grey backdrop (slightly different poses/expressions), plus a one-page retouch brief with our house rules.

We want a traditional, formal look — nothing trendy. Specifically:
1. Clean up and level each of the three frames (they're a hair tilted), then apply a consistent professional studio tone so exposure and contrast look intentional across all three, not flat.
2. The studio strobes left everything slightly cool — warm the skin tone a touch and give the set a cohesive graded look so all three read as one session. Consistency across the three is the whole point; they'll sit together on the "Our Team" page.
3. Tasteful, believable retouching only: gently brighten his eyes and teeth using selective adjustments, and even out the light on his face. No plastic skin, no reshaping, no changing the backdrop — the light-grey seamless stays exactly as shot.
4. Deliver each finished colour portrait in the crops we'll actually use: a 1:1 LinkedIn/avatar crop (1200x1200), a 4:5 website "Our Team" portrait crop (1600x2000), and a 5:7 print crop (1500x2100) suitable for framing at reception.
5. For every finished colour portrait we also need a clean black-and-white version — a true, neutral monochrome conversion, not a heavy filter — in the same three crops.
6. Deliver the finished colour set and the clean B&W set together as one consistently-named package, organised so we can view the colour and B&W versions of each frame side by side.

Turnaround within the week, please. Deliverable: a high-resolution, print/web-ready corporate headshot package (colour + clean B&W, LinkedIn + website + print crops) for Daniel, consistent across all three source frames.

Give the raw band press photo a bold two-tone (duotone) FX treatment, vectorize the supplied Nocturne Sessions wordmark, then run the client's authored InDesign gig-poster template through a data-merge against the event-copy CSV to export a print-ready PDF and a high-res JPEG.
Full brief
The Nocturne Sessions, a fictional indie synth-noir act, is releasing a new EP and needs its launch gig poster finished for print and social. The band has handed off an authored InDesign poster template (nocturne_poster_template.pdf), laid out A2 portrait with a full-bleed hero-photo frame, a wordmark frame, and real InDesign data-merge fields (<<title>>, <<venue>>, <<date>>, <<support>>, <<presale>>). They also supply one raw press photo of the trio (shot on a phone in a dim rehearsal room — slightly tilted, flat/dull, cool white balance, a cluttered gear-strewn background), a flat raster promo wordmark PNG that reads "THE NOCTURNE SESSIONS," and a one-row CSV holding the show copy. The band's brief calls for "a clean modern aesthetic—nothing vintage—powered by bright, bold colours that jump off the screen and still look sharp in print," and the poster's art direction is a classic bold two-tone (duotone) gig-poster look: the hero photo rendered in just two punchy brand inks (deep indigo shadows, hot magenta highlights) rather than full colour, so it reads instantly at both A2 wall size and Instagram thumbnail size. The job: (1) prep the raw press photo — straighten the tilted frame, auto-tone the flat exposure, and push contrast hard so the two-tone mapping has clean separation between shadow and highlight; (2) convert the prepped photo to a bold duotone — first flatten it to a single-ink monochromatic base tint in the indigo shadow ink across the whole frame, then lay the hot-magenta brand ink over it as a whole-image color overlay in a lighten/screen blend so only the brighter pixels shift toward magenta, producing the two-ink poster hero; add a fine grain so the flat inks don't band on large-format print; crop it to the poster frame's ratio; (3) vectorize the flat wordmark PNG into a clean SVG so the "NOCTURNE SESSIONS" word-mark stays razor-sharp at A2 and can be reused on merch/posters exactly as the brief asks; (4) recommend a modern condensed display font pairing for the show copy so the template's type reads as clean and bold; (5) upload the duotoned hero and the vector wordmark, then run the client's authored .indd through InDesign data-merge against the event-copy CSV so the title/venue/date/support/presale bind into the template around the placed hero and wordmark; (6) export the bound poster to a print-ready A2 PDF (300 DPI, CMYK-intent) and a high-resolution JPEG for social. All event copy stays exactly as supplied in the CSV. Deliverables: print-ready PDF, high-res JPEG, the duotone hero PNG, and the wordmark SVG.

AO-106 Nordheim Atelier FW26 editorial poster series: duotone/halftone grayscale-cutout treatment of four runway looks into print-ready posters
Photo & Image Fashion Apparel 40 calls 3 outputs 16 checks · 6a/10e ▼
Cut four raw runway looks off their backgrounds, drive each to a consistent grayscale duotone/halftone editorial treatment with grain and a signature yellow accent, vectorize the wordmark, and run the client's authored InDesign poster template through a data-merge to produce four print-ready poster PDFs and high-res JPEGs.
Full brief
Nordheim Atelier, an independent Scandinavian fashion label, is launching its FW26 "Concrete Season" capsule and needs a four-poster editorial series finished for its flagship windows and press kit. The look is fixed and non-negotiable: a monochrome documentary-explainer / investigative-magazine aesthetic built on grayscale cutout photography, a bold halftone print-screen texture, subtle film grain, and one signature warm-yellow ink accent — the same visual system across all four posters so they read as a set.

We are handing off: an authored InDesign poster template (poster_template.pdf) laid out at A2 portrait (420x594mm) with one full-height image frame, a headline block, a look-credit block, and real data-merge fields (<<look_no>>, <<look_title>>, <<fabric_credit>>, <<stylist_credit>>); four raw runway photos shot backstage (flat, mixed venue lighting, distracting backstage clutter behind each model); our flat wordmark as a PNG; and a CSV of the four looks' titles and credits. The photos are unusable as-shot — busy backgrounds, dull flat tone, tilted horizons.

The job: (1) isolate each of the four looks cleanly off its cluttered backstage background so the garment reads as the hero on a clean plate; (2) drive every cutout to the identical editorial treatment — desaturate to grayscale, map to a two-ink duotone (near-black shadow #1A1A1A to soft paper-white highlight) via a monochromatic tint, apply the signature halftone print-screen dot texture, add fine film grain for a printed-matter feel, and warm every frame a touch toward our house yellow so none of them ever reads as cold pure-grey — the warm accent applied identically to all four; (3) crop all four consistently to the template's tall image frame; (4) vectorize the flat wordmark PNG into a clean SVG so it stays razor-sharp at A2; (5) upload all prepped assets, then run our authored .indd through InDesign data-merge against the credits CSV so each poster's look number / title / fabric + stylist credit bind into the layout with the treated image placed; (6) export each bound poster to a print-ready ~300 DPI PDF and a high-res JPEG. Consistency across the four is the whole point — every step of the treatment, including the warm-yellow accent, must be applied identically to each look.

AO-107 Deli & Dough Uber Eats hero banner: grade + cut out four supplied deli shots, source a butcher-paper backdrop, vectorize the wordmark, and bind into an authored 2880x2304 banner template for print-ready export
Photo & Image Food, Hospitality & Travel 28 calls 3 outputs 15 checks · 5a/10e ▼
Grade four raw deli photos to one cohesive gritty-warm look, cut the hero sandwich onto transparency, source a butcher-paper backdrop, vectorize the Deli & Dough wordmark, and bind all the prepped parts into the client's authored 2880x2304 Illustrator banner template to export a print-ready Uber Eats hero banner.
Full brief
Deli & Dough is a scrappy New-York-style sandwich shop in Western Sydney — gritty, bold, a little chaotic, think NY deli meets Nonna's kitchen meets street culture, not polished or corporate. We're setting up our Uber Eats storefront and need our hero banner finished. We already have the assets; they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in one image — one cohesive, intentional photo, NOT a collage. Here is the hand-off: (1) an authored Adobe Illustrator banner template (banner_template.ai) built to EXACTLY 2880px wide x 2304px high (the Uber Eats hero spec), containing named placement frames — a full-bleed background frame, a hero-sandwich frame, three supporting food frames, and a wordmark frame — plus a small data-merge slug row so the tagline/handle text binds in; (2) four raw phone-shot deli photos — the hero pastrami-on-rye stacked high, a supporting Italian sub, a supporting basket of house pickles, and a supporting drip-coffee cup; (3) our wordmark as a flat cream-on-red PNG; (4) direction to back everything on a gritty butcher-paper / deli-counter texture. The four photos are inconsistent as shot: different white balance (some cool, some warm), tilted, dull and flat, busy backgrounds. The job: (a) grade all four to ONE consistent gritty-warm deli look — straighten, auto-tone, warm the white balance, lift the shadows/contrast, push vibrance a touch, and lock the look with a single shared preset so they truly read as the same shoot; crop each to the frame ratios the template expects; (b) lift the hero pastrami sandwich cleanly onto a transparent background so it drops onto the butcher-paper backdrop without a hard rectangular photo edge (that hard edge is what makes it look like a collage); (c) source and license a rustic butcher-paper/deli-counter backdrop texture from Adobe Stock; (d) vectorize the flat wordmark PNG into a clean SVG so it stays razor-sharp at banner size; (e) upload the prepped parts and run our authored .ai template through a data-merge so each graded photo, the cutout hero, the vector wordmark, the backdrop, and the tagline slug bind into their named frames; (f) export the bound banner to a print-ready PNG and a max-quality JPEG at EXACTLY 2880x2304. Keep it gritty and warm; do not make it clean-corporate.

AO-109 Kantyna Nova website photo grade: batch-retouch 8 raw restaurant food photos to a cohesive premium look + desktop/mobile crops
Photo & Image Food, Restaurant & Beverage 38 calls 4 outputs 13 checks · 5a/8e ▼
Batch-retouch eight raw restaurant food photos to one cohesive premium color grade, straightened and cleaned up, then deliver desktop (16:9) and mobile (4:5) crops of each, organised into a clean hand-off folder structure.
Full brief
Kantyna Nova, a modern Polish comfort-food restaurant and catering brand, is launching a new website and needs its food photography brought up to a premium, cohesive standard. The owner, Marta Zawadzka, has handed off eight raw phone-and-DSLR shots straight from a shoot day: two hero plates (a bowl of pierogi with browned onions, a golden schnitzel platter), a bright beet-and-goat-cheese salad, a hearty bowl of zurek soup, a slice of layered sernik cheesecake, a flat-lay of a catering grazing spread, a bar shot of a craft kompot drink, and a wide interior shot of the dining room. As-shot they are inconsistent and unappetizing: several are slightly tilted, most are flat and underexposed with a cool/greenish canteen-lighting cast, backgrounds are busy, and the colours drift from photo to photo so they would never read as one brand. The job is a pure retouch/grade edit (no layout, no new imagery): (1) straighten anything tilted and auto-tone every shot to a clean baseline; (2) establish ONE cohesive premium look on the lead hero — warm the white balance off the canteen green, lift the shadows, push vibrance so food reads rich and appetizing, boost contrast, and settle on a reusable food-grade preset so the whole set can be aligned to one named look; (3) apply that same preset across all remaining shots so the full set looks graded together, with per-shot exposure nudges where a frame is darker; (4) throw the busiest backgrounds gently out of focus with a subject-aware background depth-of-field lens blur (keeps the plate/glass sharp, softens the clutter behind it) so the food/subject reads as hero while keeping a natural look; (5) crop-and-resize each graded image into TWO matched deliverables — a desktop hero crop at 16:9 (1920x1080) and a mobile crop at 4:5 (1080x1350) — so the site has correctly-composed assets for both breakpoints without stretching or upscaling (the one exception is the kompot bar shot: it was framed portrait at 1344x2016, whose largest 16:9 crop is 1344x756, so its desktop hero is delivered at 1344x756 rather than being enlarged to 1920x1080). Keep everything natural — no plastic over-processing. Deliverables: sixteen graded, correctly-cropped JPEGs (8 photos x desktop + mobile), organised in a clean folder structure (desktop/ and mobile/ subfolders) for hand-off. Brand direction: warm, rich, premium, appetizing; consistent grade across every image; natural, not garish.

Full brief
Hello -- I run a small family-history blog called Meadowlark Memory Lane and I have one very special photo I'd love professionally restored. It's a personal keepsake and means a lot to me: a color snapshot of my grandparents and my mother as a little girl, taken in a portrait studio in the mid-1970s. The physical print has aged badly and I've had it scanned at high resolution on a flatbed so you can work from the digital file.

The supplied scan (meadowlark_family_keepsake_1975.png) has these problems: the whole image has gone warm/orange and flat -- the color has faded and lost contrast; there are several fine white scratch lines and one short crease crossing the plain cream studio backdrop behind the family (they do NOT cross the faces); the scan sits very slightly crooked on the scanner bed with a thin ragged white border down one side; and overall the picture looks soft and washed out.

What I need: (1) straighten the slight scanner tilt and crop off the ragged white scan border so only the photograph remains; (2) correct the faded warm/orange color cast and recover natural, believable skin tones and clothing colors; (3) recover the faded contrast and lift overall clarity and local detail so the picture reads crisply on a framed print -- this is the "colors, details and sharpness" I care most about; (4) conceal the scratches and the crease, but ONLY where they cross the plain cream backdrop -- please colour-match that uniform area and fill the marks so they disappear (leave the faces and figures untouched); (5) add a very light film grain over the restored areas so the cleaned-up backdrop patch doesn't look plastic or smoothed against the original photographic texture; (6) deliver a clean, true-A4 file at 2480x3508 px / 300 DPI so I can send it straight to the print lab and frame it.

Deliverable: the single restored keepsake as a print-and-frame-ready A4 image (2480x3508 px, 300 DPI) I can send straight to the print lab and frame. Please keep it looking like a genuine 1970s photograph, just healthy again -- no modern, over-processed, plastic look.

AO-116 Umbra Loft noir concert-series poster art: three archival live shots driven to a matched two-tone amber/ink duotone + halftone treatment for print and social
Photo & Image Arts Culture Music 34 calls 2 outputs 13 checks · 3a/10e ▼
Take three flat archival live-performance photos and drive all three to a matched noir two-tone (amber-highlight / deep-ink-shadow) duotone treatment with halftone texture and film grain, then deliver each as a print-ready poster-ratio image and a square social crop.
Full brief
Umbra Loft, a fictional basement live-jazz and spoken-word venue, is announcing its autumn "Midnight Sessions" concert series and wants a cohesive poster look built entirely from its own archive. They are handing off three raw archival performance photos pulled from past nights: a stand-up double-bass player under a single stage spot, a vocalist leaning into a vintage ribbon mic, and a wide shot of the trio mid-set on the low stage. As-shot the photos are unusable for a series: each is flat and dull, shot on a phone in near-dark with mixed warm house light and a cool spill from an EXIT sign, slightly tilted, with a cluttered background of cabling, monitors and audience heads. The venue's whole identity is dark, moody and cinematic, and they want the three photos driven to one signature NOIR TWO-TONE (duotone) treatment so they read instantly as a matched set at poster size on the venue wall and at Instagram-thumbnail size in the feed: deep ink-blue shadows lifting to a warm amber highlight, a subtle print-screen halftone texture so it feels like a screened gig poster, fine film grain so the flat inks don't band on large print, and darkened edges so the eye is pulled to the performer. The look must be applied IDENTICALLY to all three so the set is consistent. The job, per photo: (1) straighten the tilted frame; (2) auto-tone the flat near-dark exposure and push contrast hard so the two-tone mapping has clean separation between the lit performer and the dark room; (3) desaturate to a neutral grayscale base to kill the mixed warm/cool house-light cast; (4) flatten the grayscale to a single-ink monochromatic base tint in the deep ink-blue shadow ink across the whole frame; (5) lay the warm amber highlight ink over the whole ink-blue base as a whole-image color overlay in a lighten/screen blend so only the brighter (lit-performer) pixels shift toward amber, producing the two-ink noir duotone; (6) apply a subtle whole-image halftone dot texture for the screened-poster feel; (7) add fine film grain; (8) darken the frame edges toward the ink shadow with a whole-image color overlay in a multiply/darken blend so the composition vignettes down and the performer reads as hero; (9) crop to the venue's A2 poster ratio; and separately (10) crop the same treated frame to a 1:1 Instagram tile. Deliver, for each of the three photos, a print-ready high-resolution poster-ratio image (A2 ratio, 2896x4096px, ~175 DPI at A2) and a 1:1 social crop, all carrying the identical treatment so the three read as one matched concert-series set. No text, logo, or layout is required in these deliverables — this is the photographic treatment only; the venue will drop the finished duotone images into their own poster template afterward.

Full brief
Fizzwild Kombucha, a fictional small-batch craft kombucha brand relaunching its website, needs a cohesive set of website hero and banner graphics built entirely from licensed stock — no from-scratch illustration, no canvas expansion. The client has handed off a brand kit: a flat wordmark PNG (fizzwild_wordmark.png), a hex palette (brand teal #0E8C7F, sunburst amber #F5A623, off-white cream #FAF3E0), and a short text list of the section headers and promo copy that the dev team will typeset live (the freelancer lays in imagery + prepares the reusable wordmark, not body copy). The ask, quoting the brief, is "matching website graphics—hero images, section headers, and call-to-action spots—plus occasional banner ads for promotional campaigns," and every asset "should feel part of one cohesive family while being perfectly sized, compressed, and formatted for its destination." Deliverables and exact dimensions: (1) a desktop homepage hero at 1920x1080; (2) a mobile homepage hero at 1080x1920 built from a SECOND licensed shot (portrait crop) so the phone view is not just a squeezed desktop image; (3) an "Our Flavors" section-header strip at 1600x600; (4) a call-to-action card at 1080x1350; (5) a promotional banner at 1456x180 (leaderboard-style). Brand constraints: the whole set must read as ONE vibrant, warm, energetic family — push the color the same way across every image, warm the white balance slightly, and keep the amber/teal palette feeling present; the wordmark must stay razor-sharp wherever the dev team later places it, so vectorize it and also deliver a transparent cutout PNG. Hard sourcing rule (per the brief and the web context): because these are website heroes, each stock photo MUST be licensed at a resolution LARGER than its destination slot and then cropped/reframed DOWN to fit — never scaled up or canvas-expanded. Required content: bright bottles-of-kombucha / pouring-fizz / fresh-fruit-and-glass lifestyle imagery; a consistent warm vibrant grade across all five; all five photographic slots stay clean of baked-in text and logo so the dev team can overlay the live headline, CTA button, and wordmark on top (matching how a real web hand-off keeps text as live layers). Final handoff: a web-ready pack (correctly-sized JPEGs for the five slots, the wordmark SVG, a transparent wordmark PNG) plus a one-page style/recipe note listing the palette and the exact grade recipe so future assets stay consistent, all zipped as the web-ready hand-off pack.

AO-119 Harbor Crest Realty website visual refresh: license one large Adobe Stock architecture hero, brand-grade it, crop/reframe into desktop + tablet + mobile heroes, section headers and banner ads, and vectorize the logo for placement
Photo & Image Real Estate, Construction & Property 21 calls 10 outputs 14 checks · 4a/10e ▼
License one large Adobe Stock architecture photograph, brand-grade it to the Harbor Crest palette, then crop/reframe that single graded master into a desktop hero, tablet hero, mobile hero, two section-header strips, and two promo banner sizes, vectorize the client logo, and deliver the cohesive web-ready set with a font recommendation to a shared Creative Cloud folder.
Full brief
Harbor Crest Realty is a boutique waterfront-and-city brokerage whose website structure and copy already work, but the imagery feels dated and generic and no longer signals the premium, trustworthy feel we want. Refresh the visual layer into ONE cohesive, web-ready graphics family, all cut from a single hero look so the site feels intentional. (1) HERO SOURCE: source a high-quality, aspirational real-estate architecture photograph from Adobe Stock — a modern light-filled open living space or a clean contemporary home exterior at golden hour, no recognizable faces, no readable signage or brand marks — and license it at LARGE resolution (we need it big enough to cut multiple crops from, roughly 5000px on the long edge; do NOT stretch or AI-expand a small file). (2) BRAND GRADE: color-grade the licensed photo to our palette — primary deep harbor navy #17324B, warm sand accent #C9A66B, off-white #F5F1E8: auto-tone for a clean baseline, warm the white balance slightly toward the golden-hour sand tone, lift the shadows so interiors read open and airy, recover highlights so windows keep detail, and push vibrance just enough that the scene looks premium without being over-cooked. This graded file is the single MASTER every web slot is cut from. (3) RESPONSIVE HEROES (crop/reframe only, no expansion): from the graded master, produce a desktop hero 2560x1080 (~21:9 band), a tablet hero 1536x1024, and a mobile hero 1080x1350 (4:5 portrait) — each framed so the focal architecture survives the reframe. (4) SECTION HEADERS: cut two low-band section-header strips 1920x480 from the master for the 'Featured Listings' and 'About Us' sections. (5) PROMO BANNERS: cut two banner-ad sizes for our seasonal open-house campaign — a leaderboard 1200x628 and a square 1080x1080 — and give the square banner a subtle navy monochromatic treatment so it reads as the stylized promo variant rather than a plain photo. (6) LOGO: we'll supply our flat wordmark as a PNG; knock the background to transparency and vectorize it into a clean SVG so it stays razor-sharp placed over any of these graphics at any size. (7) HAND-OFF: recommend an on-brand heading/label typeface pairing for the mini style reference, and upload the finished web-ready set back to a shared Creative Cloud folder so the whole cohesive family lands in one place for my team. Deliverables: brand-graded master, 3 responsive hero crops, 2 section-header strips, 2 promo banners (leaderboard + square navy variant), 1 transparent logo SVG, a font-pairing note, and a shared CC folder. Everything must be perfectly sized to the dimensions above and feel part of one family.

AO-120 NOURA daily-greens DTC paid-social video ad package: UGC talking-head mashup cut with multi-hook variants, 9:16 / 1:1 / 16:9 reframes, on-brand caption / callout graphic plates, and a graded scroll-stopper thumbnail
Motion & Audio Health Wellness 26 calls 11 outputs 15 checks · 11a/4e ▼
Turn NOURA's batch of raw UGC creator talking-head clips plus product b-roll, a flat wordmark, a thumbnail hero still, a brand color reference, and a hooks/captions brief into a paid-social ad package: an AI mashup master cut plus two tighter hook-variant reels, each reframed to ~17s / 1:1 / 16:9 (same length), on-brand lower-third and callout graphic plates plus a vector logo, a fully graded scroll-stopper thumbnail, and a caption cue sheet — all copied into one handoff folder with a client share link.
Full brief
NOURA is a direct-to-consumer wellness brand — a daily greens + adaptogen powder that (in our words) 'actually tastes like something you'd drink on purpose.' We run paid social on TikTok, Instagram Reels, Meta feed and YouTube, and we're scaling our UGC ad program. For this assignment we're handing over a batch of raw creator footage and want it cut into a short-form ad package we can put straight into ad sets and A/B test.

What we're sending: (a) three raw vertical UGC talking-head clips from three different creators — a kitchen 'morning routine' take, a bathroom-mirror 'get ready with me' take, and a post-workout porch take — all shot on phones, ungraded and flat; (b) one product b-roll clip — the powder being scooped into water, stirred, condensation on the glass, the tub and a single-serve sachet on a marble counter; (c) our wordmark logo as a flat PNG; (d) a photoreal hero still of a creator holding the tub, straight off the phone (flat, dull white balance), to become the ad thumbnail / cover; (e) a brand color-reference frame representing the bright, sunny, fresh-green look we grade toward; (f) a hooks CSV listing the different opening hooks / angles / CTAs we want to test; (g) a caption-cue JSON for the on-screen captions; and (h) a brand-kit note with our colors, fonts, tone, and a compliance line (structure/function language only — NO disease or medical claims on any asset).

Deliverables we need, mapped to Adobe Creative Cloud connector tools with every step honestly tagged for execution mode:

A. VIDEO — (1) probe the raw clips so we know resolution / frame rate / duration before cutting; (2) summarize the footage + b-roll so we agree on the strongest visual moments and a logical flow, steered by our hooks CSV; (3) produce the primary deliverable — one polished ~17s UGC MASHUP master that weaves all three creators + b-roll around Hook A; (4) produce two tighter hook-variant reels as their own passes — an ~17s Hook B 'skeptic-turned-believer' cut and a ~15s Hook C 'results' cut (repurposed from the same footage, NOT exact-timestamp trims); (5) reframe: the master to 16:9 (YouTube / VSL) and 1:1 (feed), and each hook-variant reel to ~17s (TikTok / Reels / Shorts) — same length, no trimming.

B. THUMBNAIL / COVER — from the flat hero still, build a scroll-stopping graded ~17s cover: auto-tone baseline, push the bright warm brand color temperature toward our reference, shape the fresh-green + warm-skin HSL, select and pop the creator/product subject, lift the highlights for the airy look, and crop clean to 1080x1920.

C. ON-BRAND TEXT / GRAPHIC PLATES (standalone PNG / SVG references, NOT composited onto the video) — recommend an on-brand caption typeface; vectorize the wordmark to a clean SVG for the end-card and corner bug; build an opaque lower-third caption-bar plate and an opaque callout-badge plate by selecting a region on the graded canvas and solid-filling it with brand color (position/color references the editor rebuilds on the timeline); and a graded end-card the ads close on. Captions themselves ship as the supplied caption-cue sheet.

D. PACKAGING — copy all the cuts + reframes, the thumbnail, the end-card, the logo SVG, the plates, and the caption sheet into one dated handoff folder and give us a share link.

Heads-up we already understand: frame-accurate timeline cuts, animated motion graphics, burned-in captions/text, and hard transitions are a manual Premiere / After Effects finish and are OUT of scope for the automated connector pass. The automated pass delivers the AI mashup + hook variants, the reframes, the graded thumbnail and end-card, the vector logo, the caption/callout plates, and the caption sheet — the human editor does the final timeline polish, burns the captions/callouts using the plates, and locks the logo on top. Fast turnaround, lean budget — efficient workflow over flashy effects.

Full brief
Sable & Finch Realty is a boutique residential brokerage (tagline 'Homes with a story.'), and agent Priya Nadeau needs a polished listing tour for a new exclusive: 12 Heronwood Lane, Halcyon Bay - a 4 bed / 3 bath, ~3,200 sq ft modern coastal farmhouse listed at $1,275,000. She shot the walkthrough herself on a phone and a small drone and needs an editor to turn the raw footage into a professional, on-brand tour for the MLS/website plus social, delivered to spec.

Source material supplied: (1) four raw, ungraded clips - a handheld entry + open-plan living-room walkthrough, a chef's-kitchen glide, a primary-suite + ensuite pass, and an exterior clip covering the front elevation and backyard; (2) the Sable & Finch logo as a flat PNG; (3) a warm, editorial brand look-reference still representing the golden-hour, airy, deep-green look the whole piece should be graded toward; (4) a shot-list CSV noting the best moments and the room order she wants; and (5) a listing-copy CSV with the exact lower-third / card text (address, price, beds/baths/sqft, her name, phone, DRE license, CTA, tagline) and the brand hex codes (evergreen #1F3A34, brushed brass #C7A66B, warm cream #F5F0E6).

Deliverables, mapped to Adobe Creative Cloud connector tools with every step honestly tagged for execution mode:

A. VIDEO - (1) read each clip's technical metadata and summarize the footage so we agree the shot order and flow before cutting; (2) primary deliverable: assemble a polished ~90-second 16:9 MASTER by sequencing and trimming the best shots onto a timeline (1920x1080 H.264); (3) produce a punchy social sizzle as an AI best-moment cut, and reframe it to a ~17s reel and a 1:1 square social cutdown (same length, no trimming).

B. COLOR MATCH - the raw clips are flat and mixed-white-balance; because the automated connector pass does not grade video frames directly, grab a representative interior frame and grade it (auto-tone, warm toward the brand look-reference, recover the blown window highlights, shape vibrance, crop clean to 1920x1080) into a COLOR-MATCH GRADE REFERENCE the editor matches every clip to in the NLE.

C. BRAND GRAPHICS (standalone plates / references, NOT composited onto the video by the connector) - vectorize the logo to a clean SVG; recommend and resolve the brand's Adobe Fonts for the lower-thirds and cards; build an opaque lower-third bar plate (brand-evergreen solid-fill swatch/position reference for the address/price/agent bar) and an opaque end-card panel plate (cream/brass), plus a subtle brand-overlay end-card variant for the social close. The exact address/price/agent copy ships as data + the type spec so the editor rebuilds the text on the timeline.

D. THUMBNAIL - grab the exterior hero frame and grade it into a 1280x720 YouTube thumbnail with negative space for the title lockup.

E. PACKAGING - copy every final (master, reel, square, thumbnail, grade reference, logo SVG, both plates, end-card variant) plus the type spec into a dated Creative Cloud handoff folder so the whole editable-asset set stays with the project. Two rounds of feedback should be plenty.

Full brief
Ember & Oak is a fictional wood-fired neighbourhood grill, and we need a short-form social reel that makes people hungry the second it starts. This is for Instagram Reels, TikTok and Facebook. We want it fast, warm and mouth-watering — think tight cuts, live fire, steam, a cheese pull, a chocolate pour — with our menu items and prices flashing up and our logo landing at the end. Lean budget, quick turnaround.

Source material we're supplying: (1) four raw 16:9 clips straight off the camera — a wood-fired ribeye being sliced with steam rising, live flames on the grill as the chef lays steaks down, a fork twirling truffle rigatoni with a sauce/cheese pull, and warm chocolate poured over a molten dessert; every clip is flat and slightly under-exposed / cool straight out of camera and needs to be warmed up to look appetising; (2) one plated hero still of the ribeye on our dark oak table, also flat and slightly tilted, to become the cover/thumbnail; (3) our logo as a flat single-colour PNG; (4) a menu-callout CSV with the four dishes, their prices and a one-line descriptor; and (5) a brand-kit / reel brief with our colours, font feel, tagline, the on-screen hook line, the CTA and hashtags.

What we need done, mapped to Adobe Creative Cloud connector tools with every step honestly tagged for execution mode:

A. VIDEO — (1) summarise the four raw clips so we agree on the strongest moments and the sizzle order before cutting; (2) produce the master: one fast ~17s AI sizzle cut of the four clips, steered toward warm, appetising, high-energy pacing; (3) reframe that master to a 9:16 vertical reel and a 1:1 square, each SAME length (a reframe, not a re-trim); (4) QC the vertical reel's dimensions / duration / codec before handoff. NOTE up front: the actual warm colour grade on the moving footage is a manual Premiere/Lumetri finish and is OUT OF SCOPE for the automated connector pass — the connector delivers the sizzle assembly, the reframes and everything below.

B. HERO COVER / THUMBNAIL + THE WARM LOOK — from the flat plated-hero still, build the warm, appetising cover the reel opens on and that also locks the look the editor grades the footage toward: auto-tone baseline, push the white balance warm/golden, lift the highlights so the food glistens, boost the warm red/orange food tones, add overall vibrance, then select just the plated dish and pop it against the background, lay a subtle warm ember wash over the whole frame, and crop clean to a 1080x1350 portrait cover.

C. GRAPHICS — the on-brand overlays the editor keys onto the timeline (standalone plates / an animated graphic, NOT composited onto the video by us): (1) cut the plated dish out to a clean transparent PNG for the hero title card; (2) vectorise the logo to a scalable SVG for the end-card and corner bug; (3) pick on-brand display + body fonts; (4) author the title-card + end-card templates and data-merge the four menu rows (dish, price, descriptor) into per-item title-card / price-callout plates over our wood-texture background; (5) animate the logo end-card (logo reveal + CTA) into a short motion graphic.

D. BACKGROUND + DELIVERY — license a warm wood-grain texture for the card and end-card backgrounds, then deliver the full editable-asset set — all three video pieces, the cover thumbnail, the menu title-card plates, the logo SVG, the dish cutout and the animated end-card — in the Creative Cloud project folder ready for the manual Premiere finish. Two rounds of feedback should be plenty.

Source material we're supplying: (1) a ~75-second talking-head lecture clip of Dr. Nair presenting to camera at her desk — it's straight off the camera (flat/ungraded, framed a hair off-level) with a couple of dead-air pauses and a page-turn fidget we want trimmed; (2) a 1080p screen recording of the branded slide deck for this lesson (title slide, an animated growth-curve chart, and a 'Rule of 72' slide); (3) a 1080p screen recording of a spreadsheet building the compound-interest model live (the year/principal/interest/balance table filling in and a line chart growing); (4) our logo as a flat PNG; (5) a warm, clean brand look-reference still that represents the cozy, trustworthy 'study desk' look we want everything graded toward; (6) a cut-list + brand-kit brief (markdown) that lists which lecture segments are keepers vs filler, where to cut to the slide and spreadsheet b-roll, the intro/outro card copy, and the instructor lower-third text; and (7) a key-point captions sheet (JSON) with the short on-screen lines we want to reinforce each concept.

What we need, mapped to Adobe Creative Cloud connector tools with every step honestly tagged for execution mode:

A. PLAN — read the raw clips' duration/frame-rate so the cut is authored frame-accurately, working from the cut-list's keep/cut plan and teaching beats.

B. PICTURE CUT (the primary deliverable) — assemble one clean ~35s 16:9 lesson master: trim the filler/dead air from the talking head and cut between Dr. Nair and the slide-deck / spreadsheet screencast b-roll on the beats from the cut-list. (We understand hard transitions, animated motion graphics, and burned-in text are a manual finish in Premiere — the automated pass delivers the trimmed, sequenced picture cut and all the graphic plates that sit on top.)

C. SOCIAL / PROMO — a short (~15s) vertical promo highlight for Instagram/TikTok/LinkedIn to market the lesson, and a course thumbnail grabbed from the finished master.

D. THUMBNAIL + LOOK — pull a clean frame of Dr. Nair from the master and grade it into the course-catalog thumbnail (straighten, auto-tone, warm the color toward the brand look-reference, shape vibrance, crop to 1280x720), plus an on-brand series-tint variant.

E. GRAPHIC PLATES (standalone PNG/SVG references, NOT composited onto the video) — the on-brand overlays the editor rebuilds onto the timeline: an intro/outro title-card background plate (brand wash + a gold title band), an instructor lower-third bar plate, an on-screen key-point caption-strip plate, and a clean vector SVG of the logo for the cards and the corner bug. The actual headline/name/caption text is set by the editor during the finish.

F. PACKAGING — a finalized key-point captions cue sheet, and a dated Creative Cloud handoff folder that gathers every deliverable alongside the source so the project and revisions sit together.

Deliverables on approval: one 16:9 1080p lesson master (picture cut); a ~15s promo highlight; a 1280x720 course thumbnail plus a series-tint variant; intro title-card, lower-third, and caption-strip PNG plates; the logo SVG; the finalized captions JSON; and the dated handoff folder. Two rounds of revisions should be plenty.
